59.when_to_use: During functional analysis and intervention plan formulation, used to pinpoint maintaining factors and levers for change.
59.trigger: Client or family mentions "doing this makes things easier/gets attention/is praised or scolded," or clearly discernible environmental reactions immediately following the behavior.

421.skill_name: Identify and Label Key Physical Scenes and Environmental Cues
421.skill_description: Systematically identify and record high-risk locations and cues in functional analysis and situational assessment: school entrances, classrooms, dormitories, dark places, long staircases, elevators, crowded or poorly ventilated environments, as well as crowds, distance from home, hearing "earthquake," photos/names related to people, midnight threats/texts, screams, etc.; simultaneously label emotional and somatic reactions in each scene to assess their triggering effect on fear, avoidance, and insomnia, to establish an environmental trigger checklist and provide a basis for stimulus control in subsequent steps.
421.when_to_use: When creating a list of scenarios and establishing event hierarchies or environmental trigger checklists; during the physical environment assessment and situational construction phase, or before system desensitization, or when preparing to enter target scenarios.
421.trigger: When the client experiences fear, tension, avoidance, insomnia, or increased somatic reactions when encountering scenarios such as going to school, attending class, sleeping, going upstairs, taking an exam (including seating arrangements), passing by a place of threat, or dormitory routes, or when encountering cues such as crowds, distance, specific words (such as "earthquake"), photos, names, threatening texts, or screams.

314.skill_name: List and grade anxiety-inducing situations and reactions
314.skill_description: Based on the client's report and the counselor's guidance, detail specific situations related to exams, being confessed to by a girl, interpersonal interactions, or public speaking, sort each situation and identified anxiety reaction from weakest to strongest, assign scores, ensuring that each level of intensity is small enough to be counteracted by full-body relaxation, serving as the operational definition of the target reaction and the basis for system desensitization training and progress assessment.
314.when_to_use: Before or at the start of system desensitization and relaxation training, or when clearly defining the target reaction, its inducing situations, and intensity grading during training; to form a hierarchy after listing situations to guide training and assessment.
314.trigger: The client mentions exams and experiences significant anxiety, reports nervousness and avoidance when speaking in public, or feels nervous when facing a girl who has confessed; and is able to recall specific situations or anxiety reactions and provide a subjective rating for them.

434.skill_name: Systematically collect and record attitudes and reactions of important others
434.skill_description: Based on the client's narrative and multi-source observation, systematically collect and record specific reactions and evaluations from parents, teachers, classmates, partners, colleagues, etc. (such as support, criticism, mockery, education/physical punishment, dissuasion, care, or indifference), mark their impact on emotions, fear and avoidance, learning, and sleep, assess potential reinforcement or inhibition effects, incorporate school-home information into the comprehensive assessment, and provide a basis for subsequent adjustments to the family and support system.
434.when_to_use: During the social support and environmental assessment phase of initial diagnosis/assessment; or during later consultation and follow-up for treatment efficacy assessment and data verification/integration of external observations.
434.trigger: The client talks about others' supportive, critical, educational, or caring behaviors; can contact parents, teachers, classmates, counselors, or partners to obtain objective feedback; when self-report alone is insufficient to fully grasp the issue, or when others' attitudes significantly affect their emotions and behavior.

348.skill_name: List and organize stimuli situations by theme
348.skill_description: Write down in as much detail as possible the exams or interpersonal situations that have caused or might cause tension, and organize them by theme with the counselor's assistance, detailing them to specific situations such as 'being observed by others' when necessary, as foundational material for subsequent anxiety level arrangement and development of the system desensitization route.
348.when_to_use: Before the start of system desensitization or in the early stages of treatment, used to establish an individualized situation list and prepare items for grading.
348.trigger: The client can recall or anticipate specific scenes, cues, or situations that induce tension; or has been able to describe anxiety experiences related to exams or interpersonal situations.

392.skill_name: Sort into a graded sequence by anxiety intensity from low to high
392.skill_description: Based on the client's subjective anxiety scores or intensity, arrange the listed stimuli situations from weakest to strongest, selecting situations that cause almost no anxiety or only very little anxiety first, forming a uniform, operable grading sequence, serving as a roadmap and progression order for gradual imagination relaxation, reality desensitization, or system desensitization.
392.when_to_use: During the plan design phase before system desensitization, preparing to arrange graded exercises from easy to difficult.
392.trigger: Mastery of the anxiety differences or scores of various situations, needing to organize items in increasing order of difficulty into an executable sequence; or needing to clarify the starting point and progression order.

420.skill_name: Construct and annotate the timeline of problem development
420.skill_description: Guide the client to organize key events such as family, learning, and exams, along with emotional/symptom changes in chronological order, annotate onset, exacerbation, and relief points, record changes in environment and conditions, as well as past coping and treatment attempts, construct a clear developmental timeline, used for stage assessment and goal setting.
420.when_to_use: When understanding the trajectory of problem formation and evolution is needed during initial assessment and diagnosis or before developing a plan.
420.trigger: The client can continuously recall and provide information on the onset time, key events (such as exams), symptom frequency, or functional changes over time.

433.skill_name: Organize events, symptoms, and behavioral changes by timeline
433.skill_description: Review and connect key negative events with subsequent emotional, behavioral, and sleep changes along a timeline, organize the evolution of long-term symptoms and avoidance behaviors, annotate key nodes and turning points, form a sequence of event—symptom—behavior evolution, to grasp the formation and maintenance process and serve plan development.
433.when_to_use: For initial assessment or the first phase of diagnostic assessment and plan development, used to review the formation and maintenance of the problem.
433.trigger: The client can recall the sequence of events and subsequent symptom/avoidance changes, and is willing to describe the impact on life or work.

448.skill_name: Systematically collect and synthesize life history, family, and personality characteristics
448.skill_description: Systematically collect growth experiences, family parenting styles, important relationships and key events, and personality characteristics, analyze their role in problem formation and persistence, identify vulnerability and maintenance factors, understand current reaction patterns, as a basis for the developmental trajectory and stage goal setting.
448.when_to_use: In the initial assessment and case conceptualization phase, or early in diagnosis and functional analysis, when a complete developmental background needs to be established.
448.trigger: The client or family provides growth history, family, and interpersonal materials, or when the background of current reactions and long-term stable characteristics needs to be explained.

378.skill_name: Explain confidentiality, responsibilities, and sign an agreement
378.skill_description: Before formal intervention, clearly explain the nature of the counseling work, the proposed methods and principles, the implementation process, confidentiality principles, boundaries, and session rules to the client, and specify the responsibilities, rights, and obligations of both parties; based on mutual trust, answer questions, gain understanding and informed consent, sign an agreement in writing to establish a cooperative framework, reduce misunderstandings and risks, and ensure smooth implementation.
378.when_to_use: During the first session or the phase of developing/adjusting the counseling plan, for informed disclosure and rule confirmation before formal systematic intervention begins.
378.trigger: The client is unclear about the methods, principles, process, confidentiality, and boundaries, or asks questions; when a unified understanding of goals, responsibilities, and cooperation rules is needed, or when a new treatment step is about to begin and a written agreement is required.

336.skill_name: Jointly establish goals and consultation arrangements and confirm cooperation
336.skill_description: Jointly clarify short-term and long-term goals with the client, introduce the proposed methods, negotiate specific schedules such as weekly frequency, duration, time, and location, clarify assignments and cooperation requirements, and directly confirm their willingness and commitment to cooperate, forming a clear and actionable consultation plan to lay the groundwork for subsequent interventions.
336.when_to_use: At the end of the first session or after the preliminary diagnosis, during the plan discussion/determination phase, before formal consultation begins.
336.trigger: When both parties have a preliminary consensus on the issue and are preparing to enter formal consultation; when the client is unclear about the process and arrangements, asks about time and frequency, or has not yet clearly expressed willingness to cooperate; when standardizing roles, assignment requirements, and fixed arrangements is necessary.

345.skill_name: Explore and map avoidance motives, behaviors, and key consequences
345.skill_description: Around the client's fear statements, inquire about the motives for avoidance and expected consequences, enumerate specific avoidance strategies and purposes (such as filling up the schedule, changing the topic, not looking at pictures, unwillingness to attend class, not going to the dormitory, distancing from classmates), and summarize the worries (such as being laughed at, infecting friends, identity exposure leading to blame), map the behavior and context, clarify the key consequences being tried to escape, and the avoidance chain, to provide a basis for subsequent cognitive and behavioral strategies.
345.when_to_use: In the functional analysis phase, or when detailing maintenance factors and avoidance chains is needed after forming a functional hypothesis.
345.trigger: When the client expresses catastrophic worries or avoidance reasons aimed at avoiding pain; or when specific negative consequences (such as being blamed, infecting others) and corresponding avoidance strategies (such as being busy, social avoidance, quickly changing the topic, not looking at pictures, not attending class) are stated, and related scenarios and emotional experiences are reported.

370.skill_name: Identify and compare emotional relief from avoidance and long-term cost
370.skill_description: Record the immediate emotional relief brought by avoidance (such as no longer shaking, less fear) and compare it with the long-term consequences (unverified predictions, more frequent intrusive thoughts, increasing fear), assess the negative reinforcement and maintenance factors, to elucidate how avoidance maintains the problem behavior.
370.when_to_use: In the functional analysis phase or the summary phase, to locate the key consequences maintaining avoidance and elucidate the role of negative reinforcement in maintenance.
370.trigger: When the client or peers describe immediate emotional improvement after avoidance; or when experiences of intrusive thoughts becoming more frequent and fear increasing become more frequent the more avoidance occurs.

321.skill_name: Verify medical history and physical examination records to rule out organic causes
321.skill_description: Before initial diagnosis and treatment initiation, systematically verify physical illnesses and psychiatric history, review/inquire about past school physical examinations and hospital check-ups, arrange physical examinations when necessary, verify the presence of organic lesions or major physical illnesses, and record key information such as 'no organic lesions found' as a basis for safety assessment and exclusion before exposure/training, to clarify the nature of the problem and ensure treatment safety.
321.when_to_use: During the initial diagnosis and assessment phase, or before proceeding with intervention or exposure therapy; especially when the client presents somatic symptoms or has received medical examinations.
321.trigger: The first session requires confirming incomplete health status or history information; the client presents somatic manifestations such as anxiety, insomnia, palpitations, tension, poor sleep, reduced appetite; or physical examination/hospital check-up results need verification.

443.skill_name: Establish baseline and monitor treatment efficacy using SCL-90/SAS/SDS
443.skill_description: Use SCL-90 to assess symptom dimension load, SAS to quantify anxiety, and SDS to quantify depression to establish an objective baseline; conduct comparisons before and after counseling or during follow-up to assist in diagnosis, conceptualization of problems, and risk judgment, and for exposure training arrangement and efficacy tracking.
443.when_to_use: Used in the initial assessment and pre-exposure phase to understand the current psychological state and baseline; used at the end of treatment or during follow-up for effect evaluation and comparison.
443.trigger: Need an objective understanding of symptom severity or further quantification of anxiety/depression; complaints of obsessions, anxiety, fear, etc.; plan for pre-post data comparison or follow-up monitoring; client reports of low mood, sleep disturbance, chest tightness, palpitations, etc.

410.skill_name: Detail and define anxiety response in situations
410.skill_description: Guide the client to recreate the exam trigger situation, closely examine the inner thoughts and emotions and somatic changes at that time; name these reactions in the imagination of the target person or scene, and administer and provide feedback on the SCL-90 and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, forming observable elements of anxiety response, clarifying the target reaction to be confronted, and providing a target for subsequent relaxation training.
410.when_to_use: In the initial diagnosis and assessment, after selecting a target stimulus, and during the start and execution phases of each imagination exercise, to clarify problem manifestations and define target reactions.
410.trigger: Client describes their physical and mental reactions during the exam vaguely or without clear understanding; or experiences such as 'fear sensation', rapid heartbeat, blushing, trembling, tension, insomnia, unease, etc.

411.skill_name: Itemize exam situations and establish anxiety levels
411.skill_description: With the counselor's help, itemize specific scenarios that may cause tension, focusing on exams and interpersonal interactions, arrange them from weak to strong according to stimulus intensity, and assign anxiety levels (e.g., 0–100), forming a 1–6 level scale, clarifying the intensity and manifestation of reactions in different situations, defining the scope of intervention targets, and arranging subsequent steps.
411.when_to_use: In the assessment and diagnosis phase, or before preparing a systematic desensitization plan, to clarify the intensity and range of target behavior in different situations.
411.trigger: Anxiety reactions have been identified but need to be detailed by situation and intensity; or the client describes trigger situations vaguely, shows clear anxiety and avoidance in multiple scenarios, and reports significant low mood and increased tension when talking about exam situations.

309.skill_name: Record and compare changes in SCL-90, SAS, SDS scores before and after
309.skill_description: Administer and record SCL-90 factors and total score, and SAS/SDS standard scores at the initial assessment and end of intervention or phase assessment; retain baseline and retest, compare numerical changes before and after counseling (e.g., SAS65 decreased to 53, anxiety factor 2.9 decreased to 1.4), quantify the relief of anxiety, depression, and overall symptoms, evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention, and provide a basis for adjusting the plan.
309.when_to_use: At the initial assessment to establish a baseline, phase assessments, and at the end of consolidation/termination; used for pre-post comparison of changes after completing the scale administration and retesting.
309.trigger: After completing scale administration or a phase of intervention, when needing to quantify and compare changes in anxiety, depression, and overall symptoms, verify intervention effectiveness, or judge whether to adjust the plan.

335.skill_name: Develop and use an anxiety event rating scale
335.skill_description: Collaboratively establish and use an anxiety event rating scale to record the intensity of tension/anxiety in different social/performance situations, assigning scores to each situation (e.g., using SUD 1–5 or 0–80) (such as thinking, meeting, talking, etc.) as an objective basis for baseline, training sequence, intensity adjustment, and progress monitoring.
335.when_to_use: Before and after system desensitization or anxiety-relaxation training, during the fourth session, and during homework consolidation, used to arrange exposure sequence, quantify anxiety, and monitor changes.
335.trigger: When needing to quantify and rank anxiety in different social/performance events to guide training and exposure practice, or when the client can provide tension ratings for different situations.

381.skill_name: Administer and record SAS anxiety scores for baseline and retesting
381.skill_description: Guide the client to complete the SAS test and record baseline scores, check and retest after relaxation training, record score changes (e.g., baseline 60, retest within normal range, follow-up 44), used to quantify anxiety levels and evaluate the effect of training and counseling progress.
381.when_to_use: Initial assessment, post-training check, and follow-up sessions, when quantifying anxiety and evaluating treatment efficacy is required.
381.trigger: When objectively quantifying anxiety levels or verifying the effect of relaxation training and counseling progress.

417.skill_name: Use standardized scales to record baseline and outcome and compare changes
417.skill_description: Administer and record scores on scales such as SAS, EPQ, Test Anxiety Scale (TAS), SIOSS during the initial session to establish a baseline; retest and record changes at the end of counseling or at stage evaluations (e.g., SAS73→57), quantify the improvement in indicators such as anxiety, depression, suicidal ideation, and somatization, used as a basis for effect evaluation.
417.when_to_use: To establish a baseline in the first session; during assessment and diagnosis stages and for effect evaluation/fourth session consolidation, used for before-and-after comparison.
417.trigger: When administering EPQ, SAS, Test Anxiety Scale, or SIOSS tests; or when comparing before-and-after changes, quantifying anxiety levels, or verifying the effect of counseling, when the client presents with severe anxiety, depression, or suicidal ideation.

304.skill_name: Record event—intervention—reaction chain in time sequence
304.skill_description: Continuously record key topics, therapist interventions, and the client's emotional/behavioral/somatic reactions in the chronological order of the session or event, supplementing with details of location, companions, observations, feelings, thoughts, and emotions when necessary; form a clear event—reaction chain based on the main statement and on-site observation, avoiding subjective causal explanations, used for subsequent functional analysis and plan adjustment.
304.when_to_use: During assessment, when organizing session notes or functional analysis materials, or when constructing event sequences and situational details during exposure narration.
304.trigger: When the client narrates specific events or topics such as setbacks in learning, criticism, or praise from classmates; or when significant emotional/behavioral/somatic changes occur after a particular topic or intervention in the session; or when narration begins and the client recounts starting from the point of initial awareness.

326.skill_name: Record the frequency and context of symptom occurrence
326.skill_description: In the initial assessment, summarize and document the specific times, frequency, and specific contexts of symptom occurrence; form the basic data for identifying problem roots and developing consultation plans based on information the client can recall and provide.
326.when_to_use: During the first two sessions when building a good relationship and jointly developing a plan, when symptom patterns and plan basis need to be clarified.
326.trigger: When the client can recall and provide information about the time, frequency, and scene of symptom occurrence.

361.skill_name: Clearly introduce consultation matters, process, and rules
361.skill_description: In the early stages of the session, clearly explain the consultation matters and basic rules to the client, introduce the assessment process, tests and homework arrangements, recording methods and time schedules, and explain institutional procedures and counselor qualifications, preview subsequent testing and assignments, helping them understand expectations and boundaries, reducing uncertainty and tension, and enhancing a sense of safety and cooperation.
361.when_to_use: At the beginning of the first session or before assessment/testing, used to establish safe boundaries and a cooperative framework.
361.trigger: When the client is unfamiliar with the consultation process or asks about related arrangements, appears tense, worried, or doubts the boundaries of the session.

430.skill_name: Explain confidentiality and rights/obligations and obtain consent
430.skill_description: In the first session, clearly explain confidentiality principles and exceptions, the nature and boundaries of the consultation, the rights and obligations of both parties, and the options to change counselors, referral, or termination; inform about institutional settings and potential use for supervision or research in an anonymous manner, obtain the client's informed consent or signature, correct misunderstandings about the consultation, and create a safe and trustworthy cooperative atmosphere.
430.when_to_use: During the relationship building and rules explanation stage of the initial session, when privacy and process uncertainty need to be reduced.
430.trigger: When the client is unclear about privacy and process, worried about having a mental illness, expresses concerns, or asks questions related to rights and choices.

367.skill_name: Gently guide the recall of unpleasant experiences
367.skill_description: Using gentle questioning and patient guidance, invite the client to recall unpleasant events, personality formation, and current distress; cooperate with focused listening and acceptance, allow full expression and emotional release, alleviate repression and tension, promote conversation, and enhance trust and cooperation.
367.when_to_use: In the early stages of relationship building or at the start of the first session or assessment stage, used to open topics and prompt self-disclosure and emotional expression.
367.trigger: When the client is confused about the source of the problem, narrative is stalled, or difficulty unfolding past experiences; or expresses pain, long-term repression but difficulty in expression.

366.skill_description: Patient-centered, synchronously feedback factual points and emotional experiences around the client's narrative, directly acknowledge distress and situation, respond with understanding language while maintaining non-judgmental and positive attention, reduce defensiveness and tension, encourage continued expression, laying the groundwork for subsequent information gathering and diagnosis.
366.when_to_use: In the relationship building and assessment phase of the initial session, when the client is tense or needs to be understood and supported.
366.trigger: Client exhibits shyness, tension, head-down silence, gaze avoidance, statements of being publicly criticized, or inescapable compulsive behaviors, accompanied by anxiety, grievance, or self-doubt.

412.skill_name: Reviewing Homework and Affirming Specific Progress
412.skill_description: During homework feedback and progress review sessions, accept and affirm the client's experience and effort, specify positive changes and gains, provide realistic encouragement and positive feedback, reinforce self-efficacy and positive experiences, solidify trust and cooperation, support their continued practice of learned strategies and activities.
412.when_to_use: During homework feedback or phase summaries in subsequent sessions, after the client has completed exercises, faced fears, or reported behavioral improvements and progress.
412.trigger: Client reports on homework completion and subjective feelings, describes specific changes such as improved sleep, reduced tension, participation in activities, or expresses self-doubt and withdrawal tendencies.

315.skill_name: Recording Observations of Appearance, Mental State, and Non-verbal Cues During Sessions
315.skill_description: During the entry and session, directly observe and record clothing neatness, complexion and demeanor, level of speech tension, and mental state (clear consciousness, logical thinking, fluent speech, presence of hallucinations or delusions), and note non-verbal and emotional changes such as sighs, staring, accelerated speech rate, especially when discussing sensitive topics like learning and exams, to supplement self-report, verify the intensity of anxiety or depression, and provide basis for assessment and subsequent plans.
315.when_to_use: In the diagnostic phase of the initial session and in the opening of subsequent visits or sessions; when discussing core topics related to learning or exams.
315.trigger: Client enters the consultation room and begins to communicate; topic shifts to exams or interpersonal situations with significant emotional or behavioral fluctuations, or visible signs such as sighs, staring, depressed demeanor, accelerated speech rate, pale complexion, or speaking tension.

316.skill_name: Collecting and Recording Corroborating Observations of Others' Reports
316.skill_description: Inquire and record specific observations from roommates, classmates, etc., regarding their recent status (such as poor performance in class, insomnia, studying alone, significantly depressed mood when talking about exams), cross-validate and refine the behavioral profile with the therapist's direct observations.
316.when_to_use: During the diagnostic phase and data refinement, used to supplement the client's self-report and the therapist's observations.
316.trigger: When there is inconsistency between the client's self-report and on-site observations, or when a more comprehensive understanding of their daily behavior is needed.

442.skill_name: Observation of Initial Behavior, Emotion, and Nonverbal Cues
442.skill_description: Observe and record visible indicators such as appearance and attire, level of tension, thought and expression, responsiveness and speech rate, posture and gait during the initial meeting and opening of the meeting, and capture reactions such as inability to make eye contact, blushing, hoarse voice, soft speaking, restlessness, hand rubbing, crying, to form a baseline and initial impression, to verify reports from the homeroom teacher and parents, and to guide assessment and subsequent intervention.
442.when_to_use: Used during the first meeting or opening of a meeting, or when discussing key topics in follow-up meetings, to establish a baseline and form a preliminary impression.
442.trigger: When starting face-to-face conversation with the visitor, their appearance and emotional reactions are directly observable; when entering the counseling room, sitting down, or discussing separation and accommodation situations when noticeable reactions occur.

317.skill_name: Verifying and Recording Symptom Duration, Intensity, and Functional Impact
317.skill_description: Systematically ask and record the duration of symptoms and the onset point (e.g., anxiety for two weeks, insomnia for one week, lasting over a year), mark situational and intensity indicators (level of tension, number of distractions, occasional tension but short duration), and record affected life domains (sleep disturbance, reduced learning efficiency, interpersonal conflict, decreased appetite, difficulty concentrating), establish a comparable baseline to assess generality and severity.
317.when_to_use: During the initial assessment and diagnosis phase or when establishing a baseline, used to characterize the duration, intensity, generality, and functional impact of symptoms.
317.trigger: When the visitor describes the level of tension, duration, or changes in distraction; reports persistent anxiety/insomnia and impact on learning/relationships but not quantified; or points to the onset of a specific event (e.g., job rejection).

398.skill_name: Using Standard Scales to Quantify Symptom Intensity and Change
398.skill_description: Administer and record total scores/standard scores and factor scores from scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, and use EPQ, Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, or SIOSS when necessary, establish a quantitative baseline for anxiety, fear, depression, etc., and re-test at subsequent key points to compare changes, used to assess treatment efficacy and guide intervention adjustments.
398.when_to_use: During the initial assessment and phase-wise follow-up or case closure review, used to quantify symptom intensity and compare before-and-after changes.
398.trigger: When objective quantification of anxiety/fear/depression levels or assessment of intervention effect is needed; when the visitor reports significant anxiety or accompanying physical symptoms; or when psychological tests have been completed/the visitor is willing to cooperate.

338.skill_name: Recording Frequency and Duration of Symptoms in Different Contexts
338.skill_description: Systematically ask about the first and most recent episode, record the frequency and duration of occurrence in different scenarios (daytime classroom, nighttime sleep, during exams, free time), summarize specific event counts and durations (e.g., two brief fainting spells, each about fifteen minutes), use behavioral recording method to count the frequency and duration of target behaviors during specified periods (e.g., holding father for about 15 minutes, crying for about 30 minutes), and note avoidance and generalization effects, forming a quantitative baseline for follow-up comparison.
338.when_to_use: In the initial assessment and follow-up phases, used to establish or update the frequency and duration baseline of problem behaviors.
338.trigger: When the visitor or counselor can provide specific episode counts and durations; reports symptom frequency in free time or nighttime sleep; when the severity and change in observable behaviors such as crying, refusal to study, clinging, etc., need to be quantified.

301.skill_name: Measure and interpret quantitative symptom intensity and change using SCL-90 and others
301.skill_description: Administer SCL-90 before and after consultation and record factor scores and standard scores, interpret the intensity of anxiety, depression, etc., dimensions (e.g., high anxiety factor, SAS=70 severe, moderate anxiety), establish an objective baseline, and re-measure and compare changes at the end or follow-up stage, used to determine trends, assist in diagnosis, and set goals; supplement with EPQ if necessary to understand personality temperament as an assessment basis.
301.when_to_use: Establish symptom baseline during initial assessment and diagnosis, and for evaluating intervention effects and follow-up re-measurement.
301.trigger: Need to objectively quantify the intensity of chief complaints such as anxiety, depression, etc., or compare changes before and after intervention; client completes or is willing to cooperate with psychological measures; severity judgment requires scale data support.

419.skill_name: Establish and rank anxiety situation level sequence
419.skill_description: Sort the listed stimulus situations by strength and weakness, forming a sequence from "going to school tomorrow" to "sleeping in the dormitory," to characterize the anxiety intensity of different scenarios and provide a basis for subsequent exposure/system desensitization progression.
419.when_to_use: When assessing anxiety intensity in different scenarios and preparing for system desensitization.
419.trigger: Several specific scenarios are clearly defined, and the client exhibits differences in anxiety levels across these scenarios.

327.skill_name: Self-rate anxiety and set thresholds in imaginal exposure training
327.skill_description: During system desensitization/imaginal exposure, use a 0–10 or 0–100 self-rating of anxiety intensity, re-evaluate and record intensity changes after each relaxation; determine progression based on agreed thresholds (e.g., anxiety≤3 or ≤40 enters the next level, score>20 continues relaxation until the scenario is no longer tense), to monitor in real-time and guide training progression.
327.when_to_use: During system desensitization training, used when entering or ending imaginal/exposure situations to assess intensity and decide on the next level.
327.trigger: Obvious tension reaction occurs during scenario imagination or exposure; judgment on progression is needed after one relaxation; client can express current subjective anxiety with scores.

312.skill_name: Structured intake interview to collect general information and symptom history
312.skill_description: In the first session, through a structured interview and questionnaire, systematically inquire and record age, education/enrollment, family background, growth experiences, past and family medical history, symptom type and course, fear triggers and avoidance behaviors, and recent lifestyle changes, clarify help-seeking goals and timeline of exam-related events, to provide complete background information for assessment and diagnosis.
312.when_to_use: During the initial assessment and diagnosis phase, used to establish case information, organize the course and direction of help-seeking, or when existing information is scattered.
312.trigger: Client's first visit, describes distress related to exam anxiety/insomnia/decreased efficiency with unclear help-seeking goals, or when the course and trigger narrative is scattered and basic information is incomplete.

334.skill_description: Assess using scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, EPQ, record total scores, number of positive items, scores for each factor and standard scores, compare with normative data when necessary, and provide preliminary analysis, quantify symptom levels such as anxiety, depression, fear, establish objective baselines, used for diagnosis, goal setting, and follow-up re-testing comparison to evaluate consultation effectiveness.
334.when_to_use: When quantifying emotional and symptom levels is required during the initial interview or assessment phase; used in the follow-up phase for re-testing and objective comparison of progress.
334.trigger: Client reports persistent complaints such as anxiety, insomnia, interpersonal difficulties, or fear, requiring objective quantification of severity and baseline establishment; or when comparing changes before and after consultation.

356.skill_name: Conduct Intake Interview System for Data Collection
356.skill_description: Collect general information, growth history, motivation for seeking help, mental and behavioral characteristics, current symptoms, and contextual clues related to the examination through an intake interview system, focusing on chief complaints, triggers, course, and functional impairment, to clarify the nature and severity of the problem, providing a basis for scale assessment and preliminary diagnosis.
356.when_to_use: During the diagnostic and relationship-building phase of the first 1–2 consultations, used to comprehensively understand background and problem clues, clarify the current situation and causes.
356.trigger: Client seeks help due to sleep disturbance, tension, anxiety, etc., related to an upcoming exam, exhibits tension or fragmented narratives, requiring structured understanding.

387.skill_name: Organize Interview Data to Form Preliminary Assessment
387.skill_description: Organize and analyze intake interview information, judge the completeness of self-awareness, the presence of psychotic symptoms, sort out main problem tendencies (e.g., claustrophobia), propose diagnostic basis and severity judgment, to provide reference for subsequent plan development.
387.when_to_use: In the summary phase of the first-stage psychological assessment and diagnosis, to form preliminary judgments after basic data collection is largely complete.
387.trigger: Client can clearly express symptom characteristics, intake data collection is largely complete, requiring information integration and preliminary assessment.

432.skill_name: Fill Out Consultation Registration Form and Collect Basic Information
432.skill_description: Guide the client to complete the information/consultation registration form, systematically collect demographic data, chief complaints and motivation for seeking help, family and past history, and current distress, and explain the consultation process and regulations, responsibilities, and cooperation matters, enabling them to familiarize themselves with the rules, establish basic records and behavioral baselines, providing material for subsequent interviews, assessments, and plan development.
432.when_to_use: During the intake and assessment phase at the start of the first consultation, used to establish basic data and process consensus, form case files and baselines.
432.trigger: Client's first visit or existing data is lacking or scattered information, requiring standardized collection and familiarization with the process and rules.

416.skill_name: Intake Interview to Outline Course and Triggering Situations
416.skill_description: Use an intake interview to guide the visitor to narrate anxiety symptoms, sleep and study status changes before and after an exam, and differences between usual and the upcoming exam, focusing on clearly identifying key triggering situations (such as nervousness while studying at a desk, frequent urination), encouraging the expression of negative emotions, and refining the information with understanding and support to provide a basis for testing and diagnosis.
416.when_to_use: During the intake interview phase of the first or second interview, when comprehensively understanding exam-related experiences, course, and trigger clues is needed.
416.trigger: When the visitor recounts experiences of upcoming exam anxiety, insomnia, decreased study efficiency, etc., but the triggering conditions and specific situations are not clear or the narration is fragmented, and emotions are suppressed.

403.skill_name: Organize and record undesired behaviors, physiological reactions, and triggering situations
403.skill_description: Based on chief complaint, personal statements, others' reports, and therapist observations, systematically list undesired behaviors related to anxiety and accompanying physiological reactions (such as fear of eye contact, avoidance, blushing, trembling, repetitive speech, checking/seeking reassurance, etc.), and annotate specific occurrence scenarios and triggers; record the frequency and intensity when encountered in the situation, and investigate with familiar peers when necessary to verify, to form a profile of problematic behaviors, providing a basis for monitoring and intervention.
403.when_to_use: Used during intake/initial assessment and session observation stages until goal establishment to collect data, functional analysis, and monitoring preparation; or when recording is necessary in actual fear situations.
403.trigger: Client reports of tension, insomnia, fear, avoidance, repeated checking/seeking reassurance, or somatic discomfort in interpersonal/specific settings (such as trembling, sweating, blushing, gaze avoidance, facial twitching, etc.), which affect learning and social interaction.

354.skill_name: Constructing Anxiety Levels and Recording Contexts and Indicators
354.skill_description: Jointly list situations that induce anxiety such as exams, social settings, or performance, rank the anxiety reactions or situations by severity into levels (e.g., 10 levels from 0–90), and annotate subjective anxiety scores for each, forming a context-indicator list, used to define intensity, monitor baseline, track changes, and select starting points for desensitization/training.
354.when_to_use: In the assessment phase before system (imaginal or real) desensitization or self-monitoring exercises, or before functional analysis and selecting training starting points.
354.trigger: When the client has multiple anxiety reactions that need differentiation by severity; when exam anxiety fluctuates greatly or the source of anxiety is difficult to specify; when there are significant differences in discomfort across different social/performance situations and the client can report subjective intensity.

339.skill_name: Establish and annotate anxiety hierarchy chart
339.skill_description: Discuss typical situations such as social, performance, or exam settings with the client, assign scores based on their subjective tension experience in different situations (e.g., 0–5, 0–10, 0–80, or 0–100), record and compare strengths and weaknesses, sort from weakest to strongest, form layered anxiety event levels, provide quantitative basis for subsequent graded desensitization and practice progression.
339.when_to_use: Before starting systematic desensitization or during the development of the hierarchy chart, when assigning scores to the subjective anxiety intensity of each typical situation and sorting from weakest to strongest.
339.trigger: Client experiences anxiety, palpitations, or other anxiety experiences in different social/performance/exam situations; there are multiple fear scenarios with varying intensities, requiring quantification and sorting.

406.skill_name: Immediate Assessment of Anxiety Baseline Upon Imagination Induction
406.skill_description: In system desensitization training, after inducing anxiety through situational imagination, immediately guide the client to self-rate their current anxiety on a standardized scale (e.g., 0-10) and record it as the baseline for this training, to be used for subsequent relaxation countermeasures and the decision to proceed to the next level.
406.when_to_use: When starting each situational imagination in system desensitization implementation or after it induces anxiety, it is necessary to grasp the immediate anxiety level and establish the baseline for the current training.
406.trigger: When the client begins to imagine a fear situation or experiences subjective and physiological reactions such as palpitations, tension, or sweating; or before entering the next level, to judge the current anxiety intensity.

288.skill_name: Re-evaluate Anxiety After Relaxation and Decide by Threshold
288.skill_description: Guide the client to enter a relaxed state, immediately re-evaluate and record subjective anxiety scores (using SUD), comparing them to before relaxation; if the score remains high (e.g., over 20), continue relaxation and re-evaluate until it reaches the lowest level or significant relief, then decide whether to proceed to the next level or the next step.
288.when_to_use: After each relaxation training session, used to compare anxiety changes before and after, determine if the level is complete, and whether to advance to the next level.
288.trigger: Client reports decreased tension or continued discomfort after completing the relaxation training; subjective score after relaxation >20, requires continued relaxation or decision to advance.

423.skill_name: Negotiate clear short-term and long-term goals and plans
423.skill_description: Based on the assessment and measurement or consultation plan, jointly negotiate clear short-term goals (such as alleviating separation anxiety, improving sleep, reducing anxiety, regular sleep schedule, repairing relationships) and long-term goals (such as improving independence and social adaptation, correcting irrational cognitions, stabilizing self-identity), describe symptom characteristics and expected outcomes, establish phased counseling goals and implementation plans, and reach consensus as a basis for training and evaluation.
423.when_to_use: After assessment and diagnosis or in the early stages of developing a counseling plan (first to second session), when clarifying the direction of counseling and expectations is necessary.
423.trigger: Self-report, collateral report, observation, and test results have been collected; the client's description of improvement direction is vague or they ask about expected plans, and they express a desire for improvement.

402.skill_name: Specify and document near-term and long-term goals
402.skill_description: Specify goals into observable, achievable behavioral statements, reach agreement with the client, and write them into the plan and record (e.g., make eye contact with strangers, increase the number of interactions with acquaintances), adhering to requirements such as specificity, feasibility, mutual acceptance, measurability, and multi-level consistency, to make the goal a clear basis for subsequent training, self-management, and evaluation.
402.when_to_use: After assessment and diagnosis, entering the consultation plan formulation or goal clarification stage, when the direction of change needs to be transformed into actionable standards.
402.trigger: Client's lack of clarity regarding specific goals or only expressing tension and anxiety; need to clarify near-term and long-term expectations and transform goals into actionable, measurable descriptions.

384.skill_name: Constructing Fear Hierarchy and Phased Exposure Goals
384.skill_description: Classify situations by anxiety level according to the client's specific symptoms, construct an individualized fear/anxiety event rating scale (e.g., 0–10 or 0–100), set each level as a staged goal, form a progressive goal sequence (e.g., taking a bus, visiting a mall, traveling out of province for a meeting, taking a high-speed train alone to visit relatives, dormitory, asking a question in class, getting food in the cafeteria, encountering a stranger), desensitize in imagination first, then gradually adapt to and overcome them in reality, and record achievement to guide the next step.
384.when_to_use: When preparing for or in the initial phase of exposure therapy or systematic desensitization, when clarifying specific scenario goals and progression order, or organizing practice steps.
384.trigger: The client reports multiple fears or avoidance scenarios with significant differences in tension; or there is an existing list of scenarios scored by fear level, and there is concern about coping with new outings, requiring graded training.

379.skill_name: Set and quantify daily relaxation exercises
379.skill_description: Based on consultation assignments and relaxation training instruction, clarify the frequency and duration of relaxation exercises at home (e.g., once daily or once to twice daily, 10–30 minutes each; or once every two days for 12 minutes each), perform muscle relaxation when tension occurs, record the exercise time and experience, and incorporate daily jogging to a slight sweat into the goal plan, making the practice quantifiable and trackable, reducing anxiety, and improving sleep.
379.when_to_use: During the learning relaxation techniques phase and homework assignment and consolidation period, used to transform exercises into actionable self-management goals.
379.trigger: Client needs to maintain practice outside of sessions to consolidate effects; unclear or difficult to stick to the exercise schedule; anxiety and tension during exams, sleep disturbance, or proactively asking how to practice.

305.skill_name: Reach a consultation agreement and clarify rights and obligations to form a commitment
305.skill_description: Based on introducing the nature of the consultation, confidentiality principles and exceptions, proposed methods and goals and procedural rules, clarify the rights and obligations of both parties and the practice tasks, and agree on the appointment schedule (e.g., eight sessions, twice in the first week, then once per week); after thorough communication, reach an agreement or sign a written agreement, enabling the visitor to form a clear commitment, thereby improving adherence and cooperation.
305.when_to_use: From the start of treatment until the first/second consultation, when developing or finalizing the consultation plan, a collaborative framework needs to be established and participation commitment consolidated.
305.trigger: The visitor is willing to accept treatment but needs clarification on procedures and responsibilities; requires agreeing on homework and participation requirements to strengthen a sense of responsibility; or has hesitation about execution and needs stable changes in determination.

308.skill_name: Facilitate public commitment and agreement on specific actions
308.skill_description: Facilitate the visitor to make actionable public commitments and decisions, giving change a timeline and sense of responsibility; agree on specific actions and next steps, such as calling a hotline promptly if suicidal thoughts occur, attending counseling weekly, offering a sincere apology, and confirming the next topic and intervention time during the session, to initiate follow-up plans and enhance persistence.
308.when_to_use: When establishing cooperation and initiating a plan, and at the end of each session when clarifying next steps and converting intentions into execution commitments.
308.trigger: When the visitor is willing to change but lacks persistence; when proposing continued exploration or agreeing to continue intervention needs to be converted into specific schedule and topic commitments; or when mentioning the risk of suicidal thoughts needs to be agreed upon emergency help pathways.

355.skill_name: Positive Affirmation and Encouragement in Assignment Feedback
355.skill_description: Provide timely feedback on the client's experience and progress during each assignment review and stage progress assessment, offering specific affirmation and encouragement to strengthen self-efficacy and sense of hope, maintain exercise motivation and persistence, and invite continued execution of relaxation training and reality/imagination desensitization.
355.when_to_use: During consolidation and termination of the third stage and in each assignment feedback; or when external reinforcement is needed due to fluctuations in persistence during the training process.
355.trigger: When the client completes an exercise or shows improvement and reports specific progress; or when motivation decreases or practice loosens and external affirmation and encouragement are needed.

371.skill_name: Processive encouragement and self-reinforcement during exposure and difficulties
371.skill_description: Provide specific affirmation and encouragement after each exposure (e.g., "You did very well"), emphasize that practice will become easier, enhance self-efficacy and motivation to continue exposure; explicitly point out and encourage the client to self-encourage after progress or success in training and testing, to self-reinforce behavior change and maintain motivation.
371.when_to_use: When immediate support is needed during the exposure process and after it; or when progress or success is achieved in each practice/test, self-reinforcement is needed to consolidate the change.
371.trigger: When the client pauses, cries, finds it difficult to continue, or still has residual fear during exposure; or when performing the prescribed level of practice remains relaxed, the actual test performance is normal, and feedback is good.

363.skill_name: Assigning and consistently executing homework and self-practice
363.skill_description: Translating self-management into action: Assigning and requiring continuous execution of homework and daily self-practice, such as daily relaxation training 1-2 times, rational belief review and ABC recording, scenario visualization and progressive relaxation, recording and practicing "blocking" compulsive thoughts at home, continuing relaxation and listening to hypnosis recordings, implementing job search strategies, and providing timely feedback to consolidate change, improve persistence, and self-help ability.
363.when_to_use: From treatment initiation to the third to seventh session and consolidation/follow-up phase, when the motivation needs to be translated into daily practice and sustained.
363.trigger: Client has preliminarily mastered relaxation or cognitive disputation and needs consolidation outside the session; has reached a consultation agreement and is starting intervention and needs to continue practicing and recording in daily environments; or has received a new strategy and needs to implement it into concrete actions.

393.skill_name: Build trust through equal footing, friendliness, listening, and acceptance
393.skill_description: Communicate with the client in an equal, friendly, and non-judgmental manner, focus on listening to their current situation and recording it, follow their narrative rhythm, respond with empathy and understanding to accept their feelings; clearly accept and affirm the client's anxiety and fear, reduce defensiveness and shame, create a safe and understood atmosphere, promote initial trust and cooperation, and enhance openness and persistence toward the method.
393.when_to_use: During the first consultation and early relationship building, or at the start of each session, or when the client shows tension, suspicion, or withdrawal.
393.trigger: Client appears tense, frustrated, or tentative; lowering head, fiddling with hands, slight trembling; shyness, avoiding eye contact, verbal hesitation, crying; expressing anxiety, shame, self-doubt, or concerns about the method; describing negative events and pain, or fear of interpersonal interactions.

374.skill_name: Patiently introduce consultation matters and establish conversation rules to build a sense of security
374.skill_description: While filling out the registration form, patiently introduce matters related to the consultation process and conversation rules, clarify procedures and boundaries, reduce uncertainty and anxiety, create a safe and transparent interaction atmosphere, and enhance trust in the counselor.
374.when_to_use: Initial sessions and relationship-building stages during the assessment phase.
374.trigger: When the client is unfamiliar with the consultation process, feels nervous, or is worried about rules and boundaries.

340.skill_name: Introduce consultation matters, rules, and confidentiality exceptions to clarify rights and obligations
340.skill_description: Clearly introduce consultation matters, session rules, and practice arrangements in the initial meeting, specifying frequency, time, and assignment requirements; explain consultation settings, confidentiality agreements, confidentiality exceptions, and the responsibilities and rights of both parties, and inform about potential use for supervision or research with anonymity and informed consent, to enhance predictability and controllability, reduce anxiety, and foster a framework of safety and trust.
340.when_to_use: At the start of the first consultation or session, or before the first session or entering therapy, used to establish a safety framework and basic trust.
340.trigger: Client's first visit, lack of clarity regarding consultation process, confidentiality, or rights, appearing reserved, tense, or hesitant, and asking related matters.

407.skill_name: Negotiate clear consultation goals and conduct preliminary analysis
407.skill_description: Negotiate consultation goals with the client (short-term and long-term), and make a preliminary problem analysis to help them understand 'why this is happening,' reach consensus, enhance cooperation and predictability, and lay the foundation for trust and persistence for subsequent training.
407.when_to_use: In the first session, after collecting basic information and assessments; in the early stages of counseling and before any exposure/training begins.
407.trigger: Client confusion about the causes of their distress, desire for clear goals and explanations; unclear treatment goals or anxiety avoidance, but strong motivation for help and intact self-awareness.

382.skill_name: Focused Listening, Clarification, and Empathy to Build Therapeutic Relationship
382.skill_description: Initially focus on focused listening, clarification of the client's statements, empathic responses, and active attention, combined with sincerity, respect, and understanding, to accept their narrative and emotions, creating a safe, respected, and accepted atmosphere, alleviating hesitancy and tension, promoting trust and cooperation, and facilitating information gathering and subsequent interventions.
382.when_to_use: At the start of the first session and the assessment/diagnosis phase, or during the relationship building phase or when the client's emotions are intense and anxious.
382.trigger: Client is anxious or uneasy, unclear language expression, frequent crying or restlessness; unable to make eye contact, reserved and suppressed, soft and quiet speech, feeling lonely and helpless; expressing test anxiety, separation distress, or anxiety about potential harm from their own behavior.

296.skill_name: Assigning and Checking Self-Monitoring and Relaxation Tasks
296.skill_description: During the training phase and follow-up period, assign daily one to two relaxation exercises, recording of emotional/thought/compulsion counts, and in follow-up visits, check completion, recording quality, and persistence, track emotional and physiological changes to assess self-monitoring, self-management ability, and training adherence.
296.when_to_use: For training and task components during the initial assessment to follow-up phase, used to cultivate and detect self-monitoring, self-management, and adherence.
296.trigger: Relaxation techniques have been taught or self-observation tasks have been delivered; the client submits or provides feedback on events, emotional/thought records, and practice frequency and effects, requiring checking of implementation.

286.skill_name: Identifying Self-Efficacy and Barriers to Task Performance
286.skill_description: In task follow-up and plan discussions, record feedback such as "don't believe I can do it" or "inability to concentrate," check for changes in practice frequency and regularity, identify barriers such as unformed training habits or irregular execution, assess the support needed for self-control, and adjust strategies accordingly.
286.when_to_use: Used during task follow-up and adherence assessment to clarify self-efficacy limitations and execution barriers and adjust the plan.
286.trigger: Client anxiety or doubt regarding the plan, description of difficulty with execution and failure experiences; reporting irregular practice frequency or unformed habits; need to understand their ability to record and reflect on time.

320.skill_name: Review and verify past self-control attempts and effectiveness
320.skill_description: Inquire and organize the client's past attempts at self-control and self-adjustment (such as filling time, changing the topic, avoiding people, attention shifting during exams), record the effort, duration, and the effects of short-term relief/long-term failure, to determine the basis and support needs for self-control.
320.when_to_use: Initial assessment and self-control ability analysis phase, used to understand past strategies and efficacy and to inform subsequent strategy development.
320.trigger: Client admits difficulty in control or long-term lack of effective relief; describes self-control through methods like busyness, avoidance of discussion, or social avoidance; mentions not reducing symptoms after one month of self-adjustment or difficulty self-regulating during exams.

319.skill_name: Assess self-efficacy, tolerance, and self-monitoring capacity
319.skill_description: Inquire about concerns regarding emotional dysregulation and inability to cope, and fears of persistence, combined with the quality of completing self-monitoring tasks such as "recording the number of adverse reactions and time, conflict frequency and reasons," to assess the feasibility and stability of self-efficacy, tolerance, and self-monitoring and control.
319.when_to_use: Before functional analysis and goal setting, or when needing to verify ability through task recording, used to clarify the feasibility and viability of self-efficacy and self-monitoring.
319.trigger: Client expresses concerns about losing control or being unable to tolerate contact memories, or negative expectations; recording tasks have begun and can be checked for completeness and accuracy.

405.skill_name: Assessment of Relaxation Training Execution and Adherence
405.skill_description: After teaching muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, or imagery-relaxation training, assign daily one to three practice sessions and in the feedback phase, check completion, adherence, and effectiveness (such as self-relaxation during tension, sleep improvement), to determine the level of mastery of self-regulation skills, independent application ability, and compliance.
405.when_to_use: During the homework feedback phase after relaxation training implementation and during follow-up, used to monitor adherence and self-regulation level.
405.trigger: Client reports on the frequency of practice, completion or non-completion of prescribed relaxation/desensitization exercises, or describes self-relaxation experience during tension or changes in sleep.

441.skill_name: Objective Recording of External Presentation and Anxiety Cues
441.skill_description: In the initial consultation or early assessment interview, do not interfere with the client's activities. Objectively record external behaviors such as clothing and grooming, facial expressions and eye contact, speech rate and vocal changes, frowns, tension, blushing, and simultaneously record the patient's self-report of symptoms and language used (e.g., "worry," "palpitations") and corresponding emotional changes during the interview; mark significant changes and duration when necessary to form direct observation evidence to provide a basis for subsequent assessment.
441.when_to_use: During the intake or 1st-2nd assessment/diagnostic interview, or when in-depth discussion of problem details and impact is needed, to establish an objective baseline.
441.trigger: When the client enters and begins to communicate, appearance cues in clothing and grooming, tense expressions, gaze avoidance, frowns, blushing, speech rate changes, or the use of words like "worry" or "palpitations" in speech.

295.skill_name: Observation of Mental Status and Recording of Key Items in the Setting
295.skill_description: During the initial interview and routine checks at the start of each session, directly observe and record the clarity of consciousness, emotional tone, fluency and clarity of speech, logicality of thought, presence of hallucinations or delusions, intellect and self-awareness, and motivation for seeking help, to objectively describe the mental status baseline, providing a basis for assessment and diagnosis.
295.when_to_use: During the initial consultation in the psychological assessment and diagnosis phase, and during routine status checks and observations at the start of each session.
295.trigger: Observable features such as clear or abnormal consciousness, fluent or pausing speech, or changes in emotion and thought during the process from admission to free narrative.

325.skill_name: Objective recording of nonverbal and physiological tension signals
325.skill_description: In un-intervened on-site observation, record nonverbal and physiological tension manifestations such as gaze and posture, facial expression and vocal volume, speech rate and pauses, eye avoidance, tense movements, pale or flushed complexion, frequent throat clearing, noting the on-site context, as data and a basis for functional analysis for assessing the severity of anxiety, OCD, or social phobia.
325.when_to_use: During the early observation phase of an initial diagnosis or assessment interview, upon entry, or at the start of the interview, used to establish a baseline of behavior and state.
325.trigger: Manifest signals such as gaze avoidance, inability to look directly, restraint and suppression, pale/flushed complexion, low voice, fast speech rate or pauses, blushing and panic, tense movements, frequent throat clearing.

313.skill_name: Observe and record key items of mental status
313.skill_description: Record indicators of mental status such as level of consciousness, coherence and logicality of thought, fluency and clarity of speech, self-awareness, and presence or absence of hallucinations or delusions, used to determine if psychological activity is normal and to support differential diagnosis and severity assessment of problems.
313.when_to_use: On-site observation and mental status examination during the initial diagnosis and diagnostic phase, used to assess basic psychological functioning and provide basis for ruling out psychotic disorders.
313.trigger: Presence of clear consciousness, coherent thought, fluent speech, or abnormal signs, self-awareness, etc., during admission to free narrative process.

397.skill_name: Screening and Recording the Prominence of Psychotic Symptoms
397.skill_description: Record whether hallucinations or delusions are present through direct observation and brief interaction, assess the ability to accurately describe the problem and insight, and mark positive/negative findings according to a checklist; record as "not observed" for absent obvious manifestations, used for rapid exclusion of psychotic symptoms and to inform risk assessment and consultation plan.
397.when_to_use: When performing initial assessments and routine state screenings, and during initial and important point discussions, to determine the presence of psychotic symptoms.
397.trigger: When the client reports abnormal perception/thought or unusual behavior suggesting psychosis, or during routine screening; easier to judge when the client can express and narrate clearly and continuously.

422.skill_name: Establish and advance anxiety level exercises
422.skill_description: List stimuli situations from weak to strong with the client and establish a hierarchy, start practicing from low levels in a relaxed state, advance to the next level when the current level is stable and not tense, proceed sequentially from low to high, convert graded goals into progressive exercise paths, until anxiety in high-level situations significantly decreases.
422.when_to_use: Early in developing and implementing systematic desensitization plans, used to arrange stepwise progression of treatment steps; when planning exercises in the 3rd–4th session.
422.trigger: Specific situations induce intense anxiety accompanied by physiological reactions; anxiety levels are established and basic relaxation is mastered, ready to start or advance exercises.

328.skill_name: Graded Exposure with Relaxation and Gradual Increase
328.skill_description: Start with short-term exposures in the mildest scenarios, guiding deep breathing and progressive muscle relaxation to reduce physiological arousal; experience pleasant relaxation in low-level situations, extend the exposure and increase the level as progress, repeatedly train until anxiety significantly decreases and habituation occurs.
328.when_to_use: As a preparatory and accompanying step for entering or advancing to a higher level during each stage of graded exposure.
328.trigger: When anxiety reactions such as tension, sweating, or trembling occur when entering a certain level need regulation; or when the current level is able to experience relaxation and prepare to increase training difficulty.

444.skill_name: Create a scenario hierarchy based on anxiety level
444.skill_description: Sort fears/social/test scenarios from easy to difficult according to the client's subjective anxiety intensity, and mark with scores (e.g., 0–10 or 0–100) to form a graded list and sequence, serving as a roadmap for step-by-step correction, guiding subsequent gradual exposure and system desensitization.
444.when_to_use: Before starting exposure or system desensitization, select correction steps, plan training difficulty and order; after the client has initially mastered relaxation training.
444.trigger: There are multiple fear-triggering situations and difficulty facing high-difficulty tasks directly; the client can report the anxiety intensity of each situation and is willing to undertake graded training.

330.skill_name: Arrange daily imaginal exercises and reality exposure
330.skill_description: Assign staged homework: perform 3 imaginal-relaxation exercises daily according to levels, first evoking fear in imagination and then shifting to safe, relaxing imagery; after consolidation, proceed with reality exposure according to a graded list, adapting to and overcoming each step, promoting transfer to daily life.
330.when_to_use: Between sessions, to consolidate the effect of imaginal desensitization and transition to the reality exposure phase; when direct entry into reality exposure is difficult or anxiety is high.
330.trigger: When thinking of the target scenario immediately brings up noticeable tension or thoughts like "unable to escape/no help"; the client can complete low-to-medium level exercises in imagination, requiring increased frequency and transfer to reality.

352.skill_description: Perform imaginal exposure according to levels in a relaxed state, immediately self-rate anxiety; then implement muscle relaxation or diaphragmatic breathing to enter relaxation, re-assess until the level decreases to the lowest and is maintained; proceed to the next level after confirming success at the current level, practicing 1-4 levels at a time, and recording changes to guide progress.
352.when_to_use: In every level practice of the system desensitization implementation phase and in each training process.
352.trigger: Anxiety increases when entering a certain level or does not decrease to an acceptable level; after establishing situational levels and completing relaxation training, imaginal exposure and self-rating can be performed.

347.skill_name: Extract and specify exam-related trigger cues
347.skill_description: In early assessment, based on the client's narrative and observation, extract high-frequency triggers near or during exams, such as time reminders, entering the classroom, seeing a teacher, encountering difficult problems, etc., precisely inquire about when, where, and accompanying somatic cues (such as chest tightness), and guide recall and recording to form an actionable trigger list, providing a basis for subsequent stimulus control and counter-conditioning training.
347.when_to_use: When collecting clinical data and in the early stages of diagnosis, or before constructing anxiety levels, when needing to refine and lock down exam-related trigger conditions.
347.trigger: The client experiences anxiety only during exam-related periods, or experiences tension, unease, or cognitive blockage during review, the testing environment, or time reminders; reports low mood when talking about exams/Calculus, or reports increased anxiety and somatic discomfort before results are announced.

359.skill_name: Establish and rank exam anxiety situational levels
359.skill_description: Arrange exam-related situations that induce anxiety for the client from mild to severe (e.g., hearing about an exam, taking the exam, proctor movement, others handing in papers, etc.), clarify specific triggers and intensity gradients, form a graded list, to serve as a basis for systematic desensitization and functional analysis.
359.when_to_use: During the functional analysis and level construction phase before systematic desensitization, or when preparing to construct anxiety levels.
359.trigger: The client can list multiple exam situations, and the tension level differs significantly across these situations.

418.skill_name: List and confirm specific triggering situations and element checklists
418.skill_description: Based on the case description during the assessment phase, list specific situations that trigger anxiety or crying, such as going to school tomorrow, arriving at the school gate, sleeping in the dormitory, traveling alone, going far away, shopping, and clearly define situational elements and cues such as solitude, unfamiliar environments, crowds; simultaneously confirm high-trigger items such as "thinking of that girl" or "meeting or talking to her," to form a checklist for subsequent intervention.
418.when_to_use: Initial assessment or trigger identification and grading preparation phase before system desensitization, used to clarify specific antecedent conditions.
418.trigger: Client or others report anxiety or crying occurring in scenarios such as going to school, arriving at school, accommodation, going out, riding a vehicle, or shopping; can list situations related to specific people and report obvious tension.

337.skill_name: Construct and annotate individualized anxiety rating scale
337.skill_description: Jointly list social or examination situations from low to high for the client, annotate subjective anxiety levels from 0–5 or 0–100, detail trigger conditions by specific objects and places, clarify the most likely scenarios and people that induce anxiety, to serve as the basis for systematic desensitization and exposure.
337.when_to_use: After clearly identifying symptom induction, to differentiate the intensity of triggers in different scenarios and objects, or before developing a systematic desensitization and exposure plan.
337.trigger: The client reports significantly different levels of tension in different settings or in front of different people, or shows distinct anxiety differences in different examination situations.

404.skill_name: Jointly develop and rank anxiety situation level list
404.skill_description: Arrange situations related to exams or stages from weak to strong with the client, form a 10-level or 0-5 level 'anxiety level', list specific situations and mark the level, clarify when, where, and by whom tension is triggered, to provide a basis for subsequent desensitization and stimulus control.
404.when_to_use: During the assessment phase and systematic grading, as a necessary preparation for systematic desensitization therapy and the basis for subsequent control.
404.trigger: The client can describe multiple exam or stage situations but has difficulty distinguishing strength or ranking; or experiences tension, blushing, or avoidance in social settings.

346.skill_description: Following the system de-identification steps, write down in detail any exam-related situations that have previously or could cause tension on paper, clearly specifying when, where, and what cues trigger anxiety, to serve as a basis for subsequent assessment and intervention.
346.when_to_use: In the initial analysis phase for establishing exam anxiety levels or behavioral function analysis before system de-identification.
346.trigger: The client has exam anxiety and can recall specific exam situations that provoke tension.

394.skill_name: Explain consultation matters, rules, and procedures
394.skill_description: Clearly explain the relevant matters for consultation, conversation rules, and procedures (including frequency, duration, and boundaries) during the relationship building stage; introduce the principles and methods of the proposed therapy when necessary to reduce uncertainty and anxiety, enhance safety, understanding, cooperation, and solidify the working relationship.
394.when_to_use: At the start of the first session or when clarifying rules; before session termination or transition to therapy, when a unified process and expectations are needed.
394.trigger: Client is unclear about the process, frequency, or requirements, or is tense and hesitant; when proactively asking 'how the consultation will proceed' or 'what cooperation is needed' or when cooperation needs to be obtained.

439.skill_name: Jointly Establish Goals and Plans and Structure Agenda and Tasks
439.skill_description: After completing the initial assessment, jointly clarify diagnostic, consultation goals and plans, explain the process and expectations; at the start of each session, review the previous week's situation and negotiate this session's agenda; at the end, assign homework based on the discussion to form a stable, predictable pace of cooperation and enhance engagement motivation.
439.when_to_use: In the latter half of the first session or at the end of the assessment and diagnosis phase; the start and end of each consultation are used for structured interaction and consensus building.
439.trigger: Information has been collected but the focus of the problem is unclear; the client's goals are unclear or the direction of expectation is unclear; bringing feedback on homework or asking about this arrangement; confusion about causes, desire for explanation.

360.skill_name: Introduce consultation matters and rules to establish a safety framework
360.skill_description: Proactively explain consultation matters and rules in the initial session, clarify time arrangements, procedures, and boundaries, help the visitor become familiar with the consultation context, reduce uncertainty and tension, establish a predictable interactive foundation, promote cooperation and trust.
360.when_to_use: Initial session or training start phase; assessment and relationship-building stages of the 1st to 2nd sessions, used to unify expectations and safety settings.
