360.trigger: First visit, unclear about procedures and rules, anxious or restless; proactively ask about arrangements and norms.

438.skill_name: Use empathy, sincerity, and respect to create a safe atmosphere
438.skill_description: With an attitude of acceptance, inclusion, and positive attention, combined with empathetic responses, sincere communication, and equal friendly interaction, create a relaxed and stable consulting atmosphere, alleviate tension and worry, enhance trust and engagement, and lay the foundation for subsequent assessment and training.
438.when_to_use: At the start of the assessment and diagnosis phase, during the initial contact and information gathering; a safe and supportive atmosphere needs to be established throughout the first and early sessions.
438.trigger: Client appears tense, frustrated, lacking confidence, or sensitive to inferiority; expresses worry and anxiety when discussing issues; feels uneasy even in the consulting setting.

401.skill_name: Explain treatment principles and methods and negotiate consultation plan and goals
401.skill_description: Introduce the intended treatment principles and methods, explain the process and rules, jointly determine consultation goals and actionable plans with the client, clarify expectations and roles, enhance transparency, sense of control, and motivation for participation, consolidate the initial working relationship.
401.when_to_use: When formulating a plan after the second session or initial interview; used in the first phase of the interview or at the beginning of training to familiarize with the process and methods.
401.trigger: Entering the goal setting and plan negotiation phase; client is unfamiliar with the treatment method or needs to clarify expectations and process; expresses a desire to seek treatment and expects direction.

395.skill_name: Explain and confirm the roles, rights, and obligations of both parties
395.skill_description: Clearly explain the client's rights (choice, changing consultants, reviewing plans, agreeing on time, etc.) and responsibilities (punctuality, cooperation, respect), and define the boundaries and expectations of the collaboration to establish a clear framework for cooperation to enhance a sense of security and engagement.
395.when_to_use: In the initial session to explain matters and rules, when the boundaries and expectations of cooperation need to be clarified.
395.trigger: When the client asks about rights, procedures, or when the boundaries of cooperation are unclear; when a unified understanding of roles and responsibilities is needed.

322.skill_name: Explore willingness to change and invite commitment to cooperation
322.skill_description: After explaining the methods and treatment approach, directly inquire about the visitor's motivation and desires, understand their contradictions, and invite them to make a clear verbal commitment to strengthen a sense of responsibility and a cooperative relationship, paving the way for the implementation of goals and plans and homework.
322.when_to_use: After explaining the psychological methods and treatment approach, before starting the plan; in the initial assessment and relationship building phase, before setting goals.
322.trigger: Visitor has not yet made a clear statement or motivation and expectations are unclear; expresses distress and hope for help but is uncertain.

353.skill_name: Negotiate and establish specific goals and implementation plans (including rights and obligations)
353.skill_description: Negotiate with the visitor to establish specific, measurable short-term and long-term goals, clarify methods and frequency, homework and boundaries, develop an implementation path based on assessment results; confirm and specify rights and obligations in writing when necessary to enhance a sense of security, responsibility, and cooperation stability.
353.when_to_use: First to second consultation, after diagnosis and assessment are completed; when the relationship is initially established or the second meeting clarifies the direction.
353.trigger: Both parties have consensus on the main issues, need to clarify goals and procedures; the visitor is willing to participate and is open to the methods and goals; materials have been obtained and are awaiting the plan.

429.skill_name: Explain consultation setup and confidentiality and complete informed consent
429.skill_description: Clearly explain the consultation setup and arrangements (location, time, frequency, fees, etc.), clarify the principle of confidentiality and legal exceptions, recording and use scope, and inform about potential use for supervision or research and anonymity, complete informed consent and agreement, reduce anxiety, and build trust.
429.when_to_use: At the start of the first session or during the initial contracting phase; when clarifying arrangements and reaching agreement before the first session ends.
429.trigger: First meeting, unclear about the process and confidentiality or time arrangements; anxious or asking about confidentiality and process; need to sign informed consent or confirm appointment rules.

400.skill_name: Clarify responsibilities, rights, and obligations of both parties and explain the plan process
400.skill_description: Proactively explain the responsibilities, rights, and obligations of both parties in the initial consultation, define the boundaries and expectations of the collaboration; and based on the right to know, explain the proposed consultation plan, process, and principles, to make the visitor clear about the process and roles, enhancing a sense of security and participation.
400.when_to_use: Task phase, relationship building, and rule explanation stage of the first consultation; or when the second consultation enters the consultation phase.
400.trigger: When the visitor's expectations about the process and roles are unclear at the start of the first meeting; or when they express not knowing how the consultation will proceed or request to understand the plan and principles.

388.skill_name: Focused Listening and Empathic Response to Convey Understanding and Acceptance
388.skill_description: Using focused listening, empathic reflection, and active attention, use explicit empathic statements to confirm their experience and concerns, maintain unconditional acceptance and non-judgment, allow and encourage free expression, alleviate tension and agitation, enhance the sense of being understood, trust, and safety, consolidate the therapeutic relationship.
388.when_to_use: In the initial and assessment phases, in the first two sessions or subsequent early sessions, when building or consolidating trust, supporting expression, and emotional soothing is needed.
388.trigger: Client exhibits tension, repression, restlessness, or avoidance of eye contact; worry about grades and perfection, pessimism about the future; head down silence, poor mental state; intense emotions when discussing sensitive topics; anxiety and low mood when discussing learning or exams; statements of agitation and helplessness.

357.skill_name: Explain and commit to confidentiality principles and legal exceptions
357.skill_description: In the initial meeting, clearly explain the scope of confidentiality and legal exceptions, describe the boundaries of record-keeping and use, solemnly commit to adhering to confidentiality principles and boundaries; repeat in plain language when necessary, emphasize that the information is only for consultation purposes, reduce concerns and vigilance, promote trust and cooperation.
357.when_to_use: First to second assessment and relationship building stages; when introducing rights and obligations during the first or second meeting; before entering sensitive topics or facilitating expression.
357.trigger: Client questions about information use and privacy or appears uneasy; coldness and caution, lack of eye contact, short silence; worried about leakage or blame and unwilling to express.

389.skill_name: Review and Affirm Progress, Provide Encouragement and Follow-up Guidance
389.skill_description: Systematically review the consultation process and outcomes at the end stage, affirm and encourage specific efforts and progress, assign clear and feasible homework when necessary, explain the purpose and steps, negotiate arrangements for before the exam and self-regulation methods, strengthen self-efficacy and motivation for continued practice, and conclude positively.
389.when_to_use: During consolidation and ending stages or at the end of a session, when practice ends and a phase summary is made (e.g., 6th-7th consultation).
389.trigger: Consultation outcomes are evident or scale scores decrease; the client completes practice and reports specific improvements, requiring consolidation of results and clarification of the next steps.

427.skill_name: Measure and interpret SCL-90 and SAS/SDS to establish baseline
427.skill_description: In the initial visit/first diagnosis, implement SCL-90, SAS, SDS (EPQ or Hamilton Anxiety Scale when necessary), guide completion and scoring, record total score, factor scores, raw scores, and standard scores, interpret high scores on anxiety, fear, obsessive-compulsive, depression, and somatization factors, form diagnostic basis and quantitative baseline before treatment, for subsequent intervention selection and efficacy evaluation.
427.when_to_use: In the assessment and diagnosis phase of the initial visit or first diagnosis, when quantifying symptom levels and nature is required.
427.trigger: Need to differentiate general psychological problems from anxiety/depression and quantify the degree; or the visitor reports significant anxiety, sleep/function impairment.

293.skill_name: Re-test and Comparative Assessment of Efficacy
293.skill_description: Re-administer SCL-90, SAS, and SDS at the end of counseling or at interim review, compare with pre-counseling results, compare pre- and post-scores and factor changes, assess the degree of improvement in indicators such as anxiety, depression, and somatization, and record the results, as an objective basis for counseling effectiveness and subsequent decision-making.
293.when_to_use: Summary/consolidation or termination assessment phase of sessions 5-8, used for efficacy assessment and consolidation.
293.trigger: Completion of the main intervention and self-report of improvement, or when objective verification of progress is needed to decide whether to terminate or adjust the plan.

292.skill_name: Administer and interpret SAS to establish anxiety baseline
292.skill_description: Select and administer the SAS anxiety self-report scale, guide standardized completion and scoring, record total raw score and standard score, determine severity based on the Chinese norm boundaries (50) and grading (e.g., 60–69 for moderate); when necessary, combine with SDS or EPQ to form a quantitative baseline to support diagnosis and follow-up comparison.
292.when_to_use: During the initial interview or after establishing a relationship in the psychological assessment and diagnosis phase, when quantifying anxiety levels and dimensional structure is required.
292.trigger: When the client reports anxiety symptoms such as tension, worry, insomnia, or when personality traits and anxiety levels need to be understood to formulate a plan.

436.skill_name: Determine severity based on SAS/SDS scores
436.skill_description: Administer SAS (SDS when necessary), calculate standard scores, and interpret mild/moderate/severe based on score ranges; or combine SCL-90 factor scores to determine relevant dimensions, convert assessment results into clinical levels for severity judgment, intervention planning, and efficacy tracking, and provide feedback to the visitor.
436.when_to_use: Result integration and feedback phase after assessment; or initial assessment and follow-up measurement points with anxiety as the main complaint.
436.trigger: Clinical levels must be provided after obtaining SAS/SDS scores; or quantitative determination is needed when the visitor reports significant tension, insomnia, etc.

391.skill_name: Measure and Interpret SCL-90 to Establish Symptom Baseline
391.skill_description: Administer the SCL-90 during the initial consultation, calculate the total score, number of positive items, item means, and factor/T scores, compare with normative data, and interpret results higher than the norm for anxiety, depression, obsessive-compulsive symptoms, etc., quantify symptom structure and severity, establish a comparable pre-treatment baseline for diagnosis and subsequent assessment.
391.when_to_use: During the testing phase of the first consultation or the initial assessment stage, used to establish a quantitative baseline of symptoms and functioning.
391.trigger: When quantifying anxiety, depression, and symptom structure is needed to support diagnosis; or chief complaint includes anxiety accompanied by somatization, sleep disturbance, inattention, etc.

306.skill_name: Measure and Interpret SCL-90 Factor Scores
306.skill_description: Administer SCL-90 according to the standard procedure, record total score, total mean score, number of positive items, and scores for each factor, compare with normative data, identify high-score dimensions such as obsessions, interpersonal sensitivity, anxiety, quantify symptom profile and baseline severity, provide basis for comprehensive diagnosis and intervention focus.
306.when_to_use: In the initial or early assessment phase, when a comprehensive quantification of symptom distribution and severity is needed.
306.trigger: When the client presents multidimensional symptoms or recurrent obsessive thoughts accompanied by anxiety and interpersonal sensitivity, requiring objective assessment of the current status.

302.skill_name: Re-test SCL-90 and compare with baseline to evaluate treatment efficacy
302.skill_description: Re-administer SCL-90 after the intervention or at the end stage, record and compare the change in each factor score and total score relative to baseline, analyze the magnitude and direction of improvement, objectively assess the degree of recovery in mood and functioning, used for phase-wise summary and effect verification.
302.when_to_use: At the end of the intervention phase or during key review points, used to evaluate counseling effectiveness and consolidate effects.
302.trigger: When the client reports improvement or an objective assessment of change is needed, to decide on subsequent follow-up and arrangements.

362.skill_name: Systematically collect symptom history and perform preliminary analysis
362.skill_description: Engage in in-depth conversation with the client to systematically collect symptom presentation, triggering situations, duration and intensity, avoidance strategies, and impact on learning, interpersonal, and life; organize past and unpleasant events to form a timeline and a profile of functional impairment, and perform preliminary problem analysis to help them understand "why this is happening".
362.when_to_use: During the initial assessment and comprehensive organization phase, when the basic situation and event follow-up are completed, when the nature of the problem, timeline, severity, and functional impairment are clarified.
362.trigger: When the client details distress, fear, or social tension and avoidance, impairment in learning/work function, abnormal sleep/diet, and when they can recall related experiences or specify the duration.

377.skill_name: Inquire about growth history and current life and collect their feedback
377.skill_description: Systematically inquire about birth, upbringing, learning trajectory, personality, social life, and current study/life arrangements to record personality formation and background context; simultaneously collect reflections from the consultant's observations and family members and others regarding changes, supplement chief complaints and self-report, form multi-source data, improve the comprehensiveness and credibility of the assessment.
377.when_to_use: During the data collection early and psychological assessment stages, when establishing a life history and current life profile and simultaneously collecting external information is required.
377.trigger: When establishing a holistic profile or when there are others with long-term contact who can provide objective feedback.

426.skill_name: Integration of self-report, teacher/parent reports, and in-session observation
426.skill_description: Comprehensively obtain client self-report, reports from teachers and parents, and in-session observation, recording impressions such as dressing, level of consciousness, tense expressions, polite behavior, and systematically observing verbal, facial, posture, and physiological tension cues during the interview, covering triggers, duration, and impact on learning and life, to enhance data completeness.
426.when_to_use: Assessment and diagnosis stages, especially in the initial interview and subsequent contact and full interviews.
426.trigger: Reports from a teacher or parent, requiring verification of self-report or enrichment of data sources; or when emotional fluctuations, signs of tension, and non-verbal behavioral changes occur.

329.skill_name: Interviewing class teacher, parents, and children to supplement classroom information
329.skill_description: Interview children, parents, and teachers separately to collect subjective experiences, history, and situational information, to supplement and verify observation data; and interview the class teacher to systematically understand classroom movement, crying, homework procrastination, and control status after reminders, and to organize the situation and frequency of problems.
329.when_to_use: During the initial assessment stage and early data collection or key point review, when integrating multiple perspectives is required.
329.trigger: When anxiety related to observation is noted but the cause and impact need clarification; or when specific manifestations of classroom and homework behavior and management responses need to be understood.

440.skill_name: Collect general information and family health history
440.skill_description: Systematically collect and record general information and past medical history, including gender, age, grade/major, education and marriage, occupation, family structure and economic status, growth and family history, major medical events, and family psychiatric history, and can guide the completion of registration/information forms to form a basic file to support subsequent assessment and diagnosis.
440.when_to_use: Information collection and filing stage from the initial interview/preliminary assessment to the diagnostic stage, needed when establishing an individual basic file and understanding the background of the problem.
440.trigger: When an individual file has not been established or basic information is incomplete; or when a background and health history is needed to support subsequent diagnosis and plan formulation.

299.skill_name: Guide and record chief complaint and personal statement details
299.skill_description: Guide the visitor to describe the chief complaint and personal experiences in their own words, precisely record the timeline, symptoms and duration, retain key points of the original statements, and organize details such as effort and practice duration, situations of error, current anxiety and sleep attention impairment, views on classmates and teachers, to form a symptom checklist and narrative data.
299.when_to_use: During intake interviews and the phase of chief complaint clarification and symptom assessment, and when refining subsequent data.
299.trigger: When the visitor starts actively telling about events and distress, describing anxiety, somatization manifestations and their time duration, or presenting specific distress and mentioning duration.

413.skill_name: Systematically observe and record clinical impressions during the interview
413.skill_description: Systematically observe and record non-verbal and behavioral characteristics such as facial expressions, eye contact, verbal assertiveness and silence, speech rate and verbal density, cooperative attitude, thought and self-awareness, attention, orientation and consciousness, appearance and demeanor during the interview to form a clinical impression, assisting in comprehensive judgment.
413.when_to_use: During the entire observation and recording phase of all face-to-face interviews and assessment periods.
413.trigger: Observable verbal, thought, and behavioral characteristics appear during the interview, such as tense expressions, passive communication, little eye contact, low expression, or prolonged silence.

298.skill_name: Intake Interview for Gathering General and Clinical Core Data
298.skill_description: Collect core data using an intake interview system, record basic information, symptoms and triggers, duration and impact on learning and life, understand mental status and behavioral characteristics, motivation for seeking help, and explore psychological conflicts; obtain external information such as interpersonal relationships, past treatment, and important events to form a preliminary problem map, and lay the foundation for assessment.
298.when_to_use: Data collection tasks/Understanding basic situation during the first 1-2 sessions of consultation and diagnosis stage.
298.trigger: Need to fully understand the background and current problems during the initial visit; when the visitor reports main problems, insomnia and anxiety, or details anxiety, urinary frequency, and impact on interpersonal and learning; when the trigger, duration, and motivation for seeking help need to be clarified.

303.skill_name: Negotiate and define specific near-term goals
303.skill_description: After assessment, negotiate with the client to form near-term, specific, feasible, and measurable goals, such as alleviating anxiety and palpitations/insomnia, improving sleep and emotional management, correcting irrational cognitions such as catastrophizing/overgeneralization, reducing avoidance to being able to travel alone or interact normally with others, learning relaxation and positive self-talk, and improving communication with parents and teachers; briefly explain the proposed methods and implementation plan when necessary.
303.when_to_use: After completing the assessment and diagnosis or in the latter half of the first session, entering the goal setting and plan negotiation phase.
303.trigger: Client expresses willingness to change and the core problem and affected areas are clearly defined; anxiety, insomnia, or avoidance is significant, and the client expects to obtain a specific path for improvement as soon as possible.

428.skill_name: Negotiate and Establish Long-Term Development Goals
428.skill_description: Jointly clarify long-term and ultimate direction based on recent goals: improve personal and self-concept, enhance coping ability for life anxiety and setbacks, strengthen confidence, self-reliance, and social adaptation, establish a rational and optimistic healthy mindset, serving as a guide for continuous consolidation and follow-up.
428.when_to_use: Used after clarifying short-term goals or when developing a overall consultation plan, to plan for long-term changes and consolidation phase tasks.
428.trigger: Client and parent express expectations for long-term improvement and growth, or need further enhancement of adaptation and cognition based on short-term improvements.

311.skill_name: Layered Establishment of Counseling Goals Checklist
311.skill_description: After assessment and diagnosis, layer clearly and record specific, short-term, long-term, and ultimate goals (such as self-belief, understanding anxiety sources, learning emotion management, eliminating test anxiety), correct unreasonable cognitions and behaviors, establish rational cognitions and adaptive behavioral patterns; communicate achievable expectations and form actionable plans to guide subsequent implementation.
311.when_to_use: At the end of the psychological assessment and diagnosis phase or when explaining the counseling plan; continue expanding to long-term directions after short-term goals are agreed upon.
311.trigger: When the client has clear help-seeking and direction needs, and is willing to participate in goal setting; when extending short-term relief to stable adaptation and developmental goals, or when aligning expectations for ultimate outcomes.

324.skill_name: Negotiate and clarify near-term goals and implementation plan
324.skill_description: Negotiate actionable near-term goals with the client after assessment: gradually alleviate obsessions and behaviors, reduce tension, anxiety, and depressive pessimism, improve sleep and interpersonal relationships, identify and correct irrational cognitions such as "being mocked" or "inability to perform actions"; clarify the approach using systematic desensitization, REBT, relaxation, and confidence training, and form an implementation plan.
324.when_to_use: After preliminary assessment and diagnosis, in the goal and plan negotiation phase of the first or second phase of counseling.
324.trigger: Client focuses on symptoms frequently, anxiety is significant, or interpersonal relationships are damaged, expects quick relief, and is willing to discuss feasible interventions and arrangements.

431.skill_name: Negotiate long-term goals and consolidate direction
431.skill_description: Clarify long-term goals based on recent goals: improve stress resistance, learn emotional regulation, form a rational, calm, and optimistic mindset, as a criterion for closure and consolidation direction.
431.when_to_use: Reach a long-term consensus with the client when developing a comprehensive plan.
431.trigger: The client wishes not only to alleviate current anxiety but also to improve long-term adaptation.

386.skill_name: Clarify long-term goals and development direction
386.skill_description: Jointly set long-term and ultimate goals with the client: refine individual structure and self-identity, form rational cognitions and healthy coping mechanisms, enhance psychological resilience, stress tolerance, and ability to withstand setbacks, improve interpersonal and parent-child relationships, expand social networks, establish a rational and optimistic mindset, and improve social adaptation and quality of life, serving as a guide for ongoing intervention and follow-up.
386.when_to_use: After clarifying short-term goals, during the long-term planning or goal-setting conclusion phase, and during follow-up consolidation.
386.trigger: The client expresses expectations for future adaptation and self-development, is willing to make long-term changes in cognition, relationships, and emotions, or needs to align long-term outcomes and direction.

380.skill_name: Select and explain system desensitization and REBT plan
380.skill_description: Based on the problem characteristics and assessment conclusions, select a combination of system desensitization and rational emotion therapy or focus on system desensitization, explain principles and procedures such as relaxation to replace anxiety, gradual exposure, and the ABC model to the client, discuss suitability, obtain informed consent, enhance understanding and cooperation, and lay the foundation for implementation.
380.when_to_use: During the plan development and informed consent stage, after assessment is complete and goals are clear; or when the client is willing to use behavioral techniques and a clear path is needed.
380.trigger: Need to match effective methods and enhance participation/cooperation; anxiety triggered by exams or interpersonal situations and responsive to relaxation training; client asks about or agrees to use system desensitization/REBT.

331.skill_name: Constructing Anxiety Levels and Developing Desensitization Training Framework
331.skill_description: List social/test situations and anxiety levels from low to high with the client, clarifying the grading order and goals; plan the training process (list stimuli, establish levels, combine with breathing relaxation, gradually imagine desensitization according to levels, advancing several levels at a time until no anxiety remains), serving as the blueprint and progress basis for system desensitization.
331.when_to_use: System desensitization preparation and initiation phase (such as sessions 2-4 or session 3), when system desensitization has been selected and the stimulus levels and progression path need to be clarified.
331.trigger: System desensitization needs to be conducted and the training context requires grading; the client can differentiate the tension in different situations and can order them, or reports anxiety related to campus settings.

368.skill_name: Implement graded imagination and reality exposure according to the process
368.skill_description: In system desensitization training, first conduct graded imagination exposure, progressing step-by-step according to the process of "arouse anxiety—assess—relax—reassess"; select 1–4 levels for each exercise and adjust the pace based on the response; when the low level is stable, transition to in-vivo exposure, gradually extend eye contact and interaction time, continuously monitor and adapt to anxiety situations.
368.when_to_use: During the system desensitization training process and subsequent in-vivo practice stages, when progress in imagination desensitization requires transitioning to reality exposure.
368.trigger: Typical fear scenarios have been identified and willingness to expose; anxiety induced by graded imagination requires relaxation to counteract and scoring monitoring; stable relaxation in low-level situations and willingness to attempt reality exposure.

344.skill_name: Teach and arrange relaxation training for desensitization
344.skill_description: Teach and practice techniques such as breathing/muscle relaxation, confirm mastery in the consultation room; prescribe frequency and duration for home practice (e.g., twice daily, 20 minutes each), enabling alternating relaxation in imaginal or real exposure to reduce physiological arousal, providing stable antagonistic reactions for gradual desensitization.
344.when_to_use: Before and during the initial phase of systematic desensitization, ensure the client is proficient in relaxation techniques and can apply them during training.
344.trigger: The client exhibits significant tension in imagination or exposure; continuous practice outside of sessions and demonstration during sessions are required to confirm effectiveness.

437.skill_name: Establish anxiety hierarchy and progression criteria and implement alternating relaxation
437.skill_description: Grade fear/anxiety scenarios by intensity, desensitize in imagination first, then gradually adapt to real situations one by one (e.g., bus, park, shopping mall, provincial city, high-speed rail); practice relaxation-exposure alternation in pleasant and relaxed environments, assess after each exposure with SUDS or 0-10 rating, progress only after reaching predetermined criteria (e.g., relaxation score $\le 40$ or $\le 3$), systematically reduce fear and avoidance.
437.when_to_use: During the preparation and implementation phase of systematic desensitization (e.g., fourth and subsequent sessions), when gradually conducting graded exposures and setting clear progression criteria is required.
437.trigger: Client has significant fear of specific scenarios and is willing to expose; a hierarchy has been completed or needs to be constructed; requires interactive inhibition to reduce situational anxiety and rating monitoring of progress.

369.skill_name: Develop relaxation exercise programs and schedules
369.skill_description: Teach and determine specific steps for muscle/breathing relaxation (such as lying in a comfortable position, tensing then releasing, coordinated deep breathing from top to bottom), incorporate exercises into homework, specify regular frequency and duration, such as 1–2 times daily for 20–30 minutes, or 10 minutes in the morning and evening, or about 12 minutes every two days; practice can be added anytime during tension to form a stable relaxation response.
369.when_to_use: During the program development and relaxation training phase (sessions 2–4), and when assigning homework and training plans, used to reduce tension and improve sleep.
369.trigger: Client agrees to regular practice outside of sessions; somatic anxiety such as palpitations, generalized tension, insomnia, requires consolidation and assessment through relaxation.

445.skill_name: Develop fear hierarchy and plan imagery and reality exposure
445.skill_description: List scenarios with clients according to fear intensity, mark with 0-10 or SUD score, and define the goals and boundaries for each level; desensitize in imagination first, then gradually proceed to reality exposure, combined with deep breathing and cognitive restructuring, achieve sequentially according to the established hierarchy (e.g., bus—park—mall—provincial city—high-speed rail) to systematically reduce avoidance.
445.when_to_use: In the planning phase before starting systematic desensitization (sessions 2-3), when the fear object and situation have been clarified and need to enter graded exposure training.
445.trigger: Specific anxiety-provoking scenarios have been identified and the client is willing to face them gradually; sensitive to social evaluation, anxiety triggered by returning to school; scenario list and rating data have been obtained.

294.skill_name: Set the de-sensitization process and level progression for each session
294.skill_description: Follow the process in each training: first imagine a neutral situation, then imagine the mildest fear situation; assess anxiety level—relaxation—then re-assess, until the lowest level; process 1 to 3 levels each time, adjust the pace according to the response, ensuring intensity and progression are controllable.
294.when_to_use: Before and during each training session in the system desensitization implementation phase, when intensity and pace need to be controlled.
294.trigger: Start specific desensitization training where the process and number of levels for each session need to be specified; the client reports anxiety level during practice to guide progression.

287.skill_name: Graded Imaginal Desensitization in a Relaxed State
287.skill_description: First, perform relaxation training. After entering a relaxed state, begin imaginal exposure from the lowest level. If tension occurs, stop the imagining and relax the entire body, then re-evaluate the anxiety rating. If >20, continue relaxing until no tension is present to count as Level 1. Maintain each level scenario (e.g., for about 30 seconds) and proceed to the next level.
287.when_to_use: Before each system desensitization implementation and during the gradual consolidation of desensitization training from low levels.
287.trigger: Client has entered a relaxed state and can clearly visualize the event; tension occurs in the imagined scenario or anxiety is reported; relaxation techniques are mastered and the level construction is complete.

350.skill_name: Explain and guide system desensitization process and relaxation training
350.skill_description: During the start and progression of training, explain the principles and step-by-step process of system desensitization, lead in establishing anxiety situation levels and evoking anxiety, assessment, relaxation, and re-assessment in imagination until significant reduction; explain and lead initial relaxation experiences on-site, create a relaxed environment, assign homework, and encourage continued practice, and implement after the client repeats to confirm understanding.
350.when_to_use: Before and during system desensitization or related training: Second initiation of relaxation training to the 3–6 step practice phase; when introducing new steps or assigning homework before ending.
350.trigger: Client uncertainty or doubt about the training process, first practice, or when basic relaxation preparation is mastered, to conduct graded desensitization; when anxiety is high during practice or relaxation occurs, explanation and encouragement are needed.

351.skill_name: Review practice and provide specific affirmation and encouragement
351.skill_description: Regularly review the experience and progress of relaxation and desensitization exercises, provide specific affirmation and encouragement, consolidate a sense of accomplishment and self-efficacy, assign or adjust homework and encourage continued practice to maintain motivation and consolidate effects.
351.when_to_use: In the feedback and consolidation phases after each training session, and during homework review before termination.
351.trigger: When the client completes a stage of homework or self-practice, brings in practice records and subjective experiences, or feels doubt about continuing practice.

342.skill_name: Timely affirmation of progress and conveying positive feedback to encourage persistence
342.skill_description: Specifically affirm the client's efforts, changes, and progress in the review and consolidation phase, praise positive performance and reinforce effort, convey positive evaluations from peers and teachers, commend their perseverance, encourage continued practice and application of learned material, and develop the next practice and observation plan to maintain and expand treatment effects and self-efficacy.
342.when_to_use: During the consolidation and review phases after each training session; upon task completion or when phase-wise progress occurs.
342.trigger: Client completes practice or homework, reports anxiety reduction or positive changes, submits practice results, receives positive evaluations from peers and teachers, or shows doubt about continuing training.

399.skill_name: Introduce treatment principles and goals and negotiate a plan
399.skill_description: Explain the purpose, principles, and phase arrangement of the rational emotion therapy, progressive relaxation training, exposure therapy, or system desensitization and cognitive behavioral therapy to be used; explain symptom characteristics and influencing factors, clarify achievable expected goals, negotiate and formulate a consultation plan, and implement psychoeducation to help form reasonable expectations and cooperation.
399.when_to_use: During the diagnostic phase or when determining goals and plans in the second consultation; before treatment begins or introducing new techniques.
399.trigger: Client is unclear about the treatment method and mechanism, confused or worried about the problem and the future, or has poor cooperation, requiring clarification of methods and steps.

349.skill_name: Teach muscle and breathing relaxation and assign exercises
349.skill_description: Teach muscle relaxation and slow breathing training, perform tension-relaxation contrasts in a top-down order and emphasize facial muscles, provide on-site demonstration for a full-body relaxation experience; guide comfortable sitting posture for breathing relaxation, create a relaxation response before and after imagining anxiety situations; assign daily practice of 1–2 times or 30–40 minutes per session at home, until it can be used spontaneously in daily environments to counteract anxiety.
349.when_to_use: Start the relaxation training and skill acquisition phase in the 1st–2nd consultation; in anxiety regulation stages before and during formal exposure, and when progressing through each level of desensitization.
349.trigger: When the client exhibits physiological tension such as rapid heart rate, muscle tension, or rapid breathing, or tension before and after imagining, restlessness, difficulty entering or spontaneous relaxation, requiring learning and demonstration of relaxation.

310.skill_name: Establish Anxiety Hierarchy and Progression Criteria
310.skill_description: Guide the construction of anxiety levels based on situational intensity (e.g., levels 1–6 or 10), conduct imaginal exposure in a relaxed state; monitor anxiety via self-rating and progress according to agreed thresholds (e.g., $\le 40$ points or below 3 points); if the score exceeds 20 points, continue relaxation to ensure standardized and safe progression.
310.when_to_use: When establishing the practice list and procedure instructions at the beginning of system desensitization, and when deciding whether to advance during training.
310.trigger: Client is unclear about the training process and progression standards; can distinguish anxiety intensity across different situations; reports scores or discomfort/fatigue, requiring clear progression standards.

409.skill_name: Graded imaginal exposure and repeated relaxation assessment to lowest anxiety
409.skill_description: Implement scenario imagination according to the predetermined levels, first evoke and assess anxiety, then proceed to relaxation to enter a relaxed state, then re-assess, repeat until anxiety is at its lowest; perform levels 1–3 or 1–4 each time; after each relaxation, ask about the anxiety score, if it exceeds 20 points, continue relaxation, using process-oriented guidance and encouragement to maintain practice progress.
409.when_to_use: When progressing through levels during each system desensitization training process.
409.trigger: When tension, palpitations, or other reactions occur in the imagined scenario, enter relaxation and re-assessment; after relaxation, assess anxiety or report no relief; if assessment shows anxiety has not reached the lowest level.

408.skill_name: Explanation of System Desensitization Principles and Gradation Process
408.skill_description: Explain the principles of system desensitization for combating specific fears and anxieties and the mechanism of relaxation for combating anxiety; clearly explain the gradation exposure and imaginal desensitization process: grade by scene anxiety intensity, desensitize in imagination first, then gradually adapt in reality; practice steps are: imagine arousal of anxiety—assessment—relaxation—and re-assessment, until anxiety is at its lowest, helping to form rational expectations.
408.when_to_use: Before starting system desensitization or relaxation training and during the initial phase of training, as well as in the instruction phase before each practice; before and during exposure training.
408.trigger: Client is unclear about the training purpose and method or needs to understand the method and expectations; when preparing to establish anxiety levels or start imaginal training; when unclear about the process or experiencing fear or avoidance.

341.skill_name: Guide awareness of reactions and switch to relaxation and scoring progression
341.skill_description: In imaginal desensitization training, guide the client to progressively imagine according to anxiety levels, noticing emotional and physiological reactions; when tension occurs, stop the imagination and perform full-body relaxation, allowing the body to transition from tension to relaxation, learning to replace anxiety with relaxation; ask for the anxiety score each time, and if it exceeds the agreed threshold (e.g., 20 points), continue relaxation until no longer tense before moving to the next level.
341.when_to_use: Used during each level of imaginal desensitization training and with each practice progression to manage emerging tension and anxiety reactions and establish the correct practice procedure.
341.trigger: Manifestations such as palpitations, tension, sweating, trembling, blurred vision, or staring, or difficulty in self-relaxation during practice; client reports subjective scores exceeding the threshold.

318.skill_name: Assessment of Self-Control, Coping Strategies, and Effectiveness
318.skill_description: Record past and current attempts at self-regulation and control (such as silent crying, not speaking out, finger cutting, self-motivation, phone seeking help and wrist cutting promises), identify self-restraint and active help-seeking behaviors, observe self-regulation during intense emotions and needed external cues, assess the effectiveness and limitations of each strategy, define available resources (such as response to breathing relaxation), provide basis for subsequent interventions and goals, and conduct risk management.
318.when_to_use: In the stage of functional analysis of self-control dimensions, during the assessment phase and session feedback, used to formulate alternative strategies and intervention plans.
318.trigger: Occurrence or recall of self-harm, suppressed crying, self-motivation, phone seeking help, and safety promises; or when the client describes self-control efforts, control failure, intense negative emotions, and requires observation of self-regulation and strategy effectiveness.

300.skill_name: Identification of Personality Traits and Deficits in Self-Regulation
300.skill_description: Record personality traits such as sensitivity, strong self-esteem, and self-control and cognitive characteristics such as difficulty expressing emotions, susceptibility to suggestion, and rumination, combined with learning and social functioning status, differentiate maintenance factors from available resources, assess the impact on symptoms and functioning, used to predict compliance and guide intervention focus and training selection.
300.when_to_use: In the psychological and self-control assessment phase of etiology/functional analysis, or before selecting emotion/cognitive regulation training and setting goals.
300.trigger: When the client describes personality traits and inability to alleviate anxiety, presents difficulty in emotional expression, recurrent worry, susceptibility to suggestion, or when learning and social functioning are maintained despite tension but efficiency decreases.

333.skill_name: Guide reality observation and recording of others' and self's reactions
333.skill_description: Guide the client to observe others' behaviors in real situations and record them (e.g., by writing observation diaries), compare actual attention with self-feelings, and extract the influence of environmental and social cues on anxiety, as factual basis for refining situational and environmental analysis.
333.when_to_use: During the homework implementation and feedback phase, in conjunction with attitude surveys and cognitive correction, to refine situational and environmental analysis.
333.trigger: When the client is highly tense in public, believes others are watching them, or shows differences in reaction when in front of different relational objects.

365.skill_name: Integrate observation and others' feedback to assess social functioning and attitudes
365.skill_description: Combine in-person observation with feedback from important others such as teachers, classmates, and parents, record attitudes such as encouragement, reassurance, understanding, or coldness and specific support arrangements, assess the impact on fear, avoidance, and social functioning, calibrate the client's subjective inferences about others' reactions, and enrich functional analysis evidence.
365.when_to_use: Used when collecting multi-source information during the assessment and diagnosis phase to determine the impact of social functioning and the attitudes of important others, or when examining the support system in functional analysis.
365.trigger: When receiving updates and attitudes from peers/teachers/parents, or when observing tension, decreased social participation, arrangements for reassurance, encouragement, visits, drop-offs, or praise.

332.skill_name: Integrate data and assessment to form functional conclusions and diagnoses
332.skill_description: Analyze and judge based on the duration, intensity, nature, and severity of the problem using combined interview data and psychological test results, organize typical psychological and behavioral abnormal manifestations, form conclusive statements, and provide feedback to the client, as a basis for establishing a diagnosis and subsequent goals and plans.
332.when_to_use: During the assessment and diagnosis phase or the conclusion of functional analysis, when it is necessary to clarify the nature and severity of the problem and form a conclusive statement.
332.trigger: Clinical data and scale results have been collected, the client reports symptoms such as social anxiety and avoidance, when it is necessary to clarify the diagnosis and maintenance mechanisms.

307.skill_name: Identify and Record Trigger Situations and Response Patterns
307.skill_description: Systematically collect and record specific scenarios and accompanying emotions when thoughts or fears occur, detail trigger situations and manifestation of episodes (trembling, sense of loss of control, blank mind, and autonomic symptoms) such as riding alone, crowds, classroom, record the timing and antecedents/consequences of avoidance, and characterize the situation-response association and sensitivity points.
307.when_to_use: In the phase of exploring the conditions and maintaining factors of problem occurrence, or when analyzing situations and reconstructing typical events.
307.trigger: Client reports that leisure time, before sleep, specific places or activities trigger tension, excitement, impulsivity, or avoidance, and describes accompanying physiological and behavioral reactions.

447.skill_name: Formulate functional conclusions and align with goals
447.skill_description: Collaborate with the client to integrate information such as triggering situations, core symptoms, developmental and maintenance mechanisms, condense functional statements, clarify key control variables and variables, reach consensus on 'why this is happening', to guide subsequent goal setting, intervention plans, and relapse prevention.
447.when_to_use: After key information collection is complete or before phase review, goal setting, and plan development.
447.trigger: When functional cues are complete and the behavioral chain is clear, and it is necessary to consolidate into an actionable functional explanation and reach consensus with the client.

396.skill_description: Collaboratively list specific physical and social situations that trigger fear/anxiety with the client (e.g., riding alone, bus, park, returning to school, talking to relatives), and grade them according to subjective fear/anxiety intensity, annotating the emotional and physiological reactions for each level, used for contextualized functional assessment and intervention level setting.
396.when_to_use: During the physical environment and situational analysis phase, or before establishing exposure/adaptation levels, when differentiating triggers and intensity differences is necessary.
396.trigger: When the client reports symptom differences across different settings, fear/avoidance in multiple scenarios, and difficulty focusing on a primary target or ordering.

383.skill_name: Review developmental and caregiving history to identify developmental factors
383.skill_description: Systematically gather the client’s developmental and caregiving history, such as parental separation or remarriage, long-term care by grandparents, harsh punishment, perfectionism and high expectations, limited peer relationships, academic pressure, and changes in confidence. Assess how these experiences relate to reactions such as low self-worth, loneliness, withdrawal, or interpersonal sensitivity, as context for the development of current concerns and underlying vulnerabilities.
383.when_to_use: During assessment and developmental formulation, when gathering childhood, temperament, and academic history to explain current patterns of response.
383.trigger: The client or a caregiver provides ongoing information about family disruptions, caregiving practices, school experiences, or long-term behavior.

414.skill_name: Use scales to quantify symptom severity and personality traits
414.skill_description: Under intake interview, administer scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, EPQ to quantify levels of anxiety, depression, and somatization, and personality traits, establish a comparable baseline, and re-measure and compare changes during follow-up to provide data for preliminary problem analysis, diagnostic judgment, and goal setting.
414.when_to_use: Establish baseline during the initial consultation assessment phase, and update indicators during periodic reviews.
414.trigger: When the client reports test anxiety/emotional distress, requires objective quantification of severity and scope, or needs to clarify personality traits and diagnostic basis.

415.skill_name: Establish anxiety level sequence and annotate intensity
415.skill_description: List stimulus situations related to tests or social situations with the client, arrange them from weak to strong according to the intensity of anxiety they provoke, and annotate the intensity of physiological, emotional, and cognitive reactions with subjective scores such as SUD or 0-80, to form an anxiety level, providing a structured baseline for subsequent systematic desensitization, exposure, or monitoring.
415.when_to_use: To assess reaction intensity and levels in functional analysis, or before developing a systematic desensitization/exposure plan.
415.trigger: When the client can identify different intensities of reactions such as increased heart rate, sweating, blocked thinking after mastering relaxation training or listing stimulus situations, and needs to be graded and quantified.

446.skill_name: Quantify symptom intensity and range and establish a baseline
446.skill_description: Use scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, and diagnostic criteria to record anxiety and fear-related factors and autonomic nervous system symptoms, while guiding daily behavior and emotion recording and subjective scoring, to form quantifiable baselines of frequency, intensity, range, and comparability, for intervention planning and efficacy assessment.
446.when_to_use: To establish a baseline during the assessment and situational analysis phases, and to re-measure and compare changes at the end phase.
446.trigger: When objective symptom levels or subjective descriptions fluctuate significantly; when the client is willing to complete questionnaires and perform daily recording and scoring.

289.skill_name: Record chief complaint, symptom course, and medical history
289.skill_description: Used to summarize the core distress and self-reported symptoms in the client's own words, record diurnal variations, onset time and triggers, duration and frequency, and impact on learning and life; and organize past medical visits, medication use, referral motivations, and willingness to seek help to form an overview of the problem and a checklist.
289.when_to_use: During initial assessment/first interview and diagnostic phase, when collecting the current status of problems, symptom details, and defining the reason for seeking care.
289.trigger: When the client begins to describe anxiety or other symptoms, duration and triggers (e.g., exam failure), or mentions hospitalization, doctor's diagnosis, end of medication treatment, or functional impairment.

323.skill_name: Systematically record general information and precipitating events
323.skill_description: Systematically record general information such as gender, age, grade level, body type and expression, learning and social participation, combined with general health status and family psychiatric/organic disease history, annotate key precipitating events, to establish a foundation for the record and subsequent assessment.
323.when_to_use: In the diagnostic phase of the first or second session before initial assessment, when establishing the relationship and preparing to develop a consultation plan.
323.trigger: First visit by the client with symptoms affecting learning and life, or when beginning to provide family, health history, and precipitating event information.

424.skill_name: Collect and record physical history and family psychiatric history
424.skill_description: Explicitly inquire and record past major physical illnesses and family history of mental illness/genetic diseases, combined with current psychological and behavioral manifestations, used to assist in ruling out severe psychoses and defining the nature of the problem, ensuring sufficient medical background information.
424.when_to_use: When filling out the history module during the initial assessment, or when needing to rule out organic factors and severe family psychiatric problems.
424.trigger: Unclear health history, unknown family psychiatric history, or when diagnosis needs to rule out signs of severe psychosis.

297.skill_name: Record mental status and screen for psychotic symptoms
297.skill_description: Record consciousness, speech, anxiety level, and changes in attention, sleep, and mood over the last two weeks based on mental and physical status entries, and verify intact self-awareness and the presence of hallucinations or delusions to support differential assessment.
297.when_to_use: In the initial observation and inquiry phase, or in mental status examination items before diagnosis.
297.trigger: Visible tension, lethargy, or client reports of attention and sleep problems during the interview, or the ability to clearly express and deny psychotic experiences.

372.skill_name: Collect Basic Information and Growth Family Background
372.skill_description: Systematically record gender, age, professional status, upbringing environment and family/parent-child relationships, roles and behaviors, physical illnesses and trauma history, as well as date of birth, economic status, current residence and cohabitants, personality traits and learning trajectory, to form background information required for assessment.
372.when_to_use: In the first stage of assessment and diagnosis, when establishing the therapeutic relationship and filling out basic information and background sections of the questionnaire.
372.trigger: Initial interview requires understanding basic background, or when the client begins to review their growth experiences, family, and health history.

290.skill_name: Collect important others' reports to supplement information
290.skill_description: Proactively gather descriptions of the visitor's personality, past behavior, and symptom changes from guardians or key others, record similarities and differences between reports and self-report, complete the source information, and improve the comprehensiveness and credibility of the data.
290.when_to_use: When verifying information from multiple sources and supplementing social information during the initial assessment phase.
290.trigger: Parent present or willing and able to provide information, or discrepancies between self-report and observation require corroboration.

358.skill_name: Record chief complaint, symptom characteristics, and precipitating context
358.skill_description: Accurately record the core distress and symptoms (such as dizziness, palpitations, insomnia, worry/fear), onset time and recent changes, as well as typical occurrence scenarios and precipitating events, to refine the problem profile for subsequent assessment and localization.
358.when_to_use: During the initial interview and assessment phase, fill in the chief complaint and symptom sections of the questionnaire, and before developing goals.
358.trigger: When the client actively states the current distress, fear situation, or details of an episode, mentioning clues such as test anxiety, suicidal ideation, etc.

425.skill_name: Record typical psychological and behavioral manifestations
425.skill_description: Record emotional and behavioral manifestations by time and context, such as crying, restlessness, repetitive hand rubbing, somatic discomfort, and disruptive behaviors during school accommodation, to form a problem behavior profile to support subsequent analysis and diagnosis.
425.when_to_use: Fill in the "symptoms and behaviors" section during the assessment phase or after on-site observation.
425.trigger: When the client exhibits significant emotional or somatized symptoms, or the homeroom teacher and parents report disruptive behavior and adjustment difficulties.

364.skill_name: Interview observation and recording of appearance and mental status
364.skill_description: Systematically observe and record clothing neatness, complexion and expression, tension and behavior, thought clarity, consciousness and orientation, self-awareness, and presence of hallucinations during the interview, and summarize subjective reports and personality evaluations from teachers, classmates, or family members, as objective data beyond subjective reports.
364.when_to_use: During the clinical observation phase of the first interview and the initial data collection stage, requires cross-referencing multiple sources.
364.trigger: Visible emotional fluctuations, nervous speech, anxious expression, or changes in speech rate and expression during the interview, or available external reports to relay.

373.skill_name: Record chief complaint, course, and functional impairment
373.skill_description: Detailed recording of symptoms and duration, precipitating situations and reasons for seeking help, as well as sleep, learning, and daily function impairment, including medical information when necessary, to serve as a baseline for the problem and severity judgment.
373.when_to_use: In the initial assessment phase, used to clarify the nature and severity of the problem, and before setting goals.
373.trigger: When the visitor reports fear, anxiety, or somatization symptoms, describes the duration, or mentions hospital examinations and results, and describes avoidance and functional impairment.

390.skill_name: Guide the completion of the consultation registration form and explain the process and rules
390.skill_description: Guide the visitor to complete the consultation registration form, standardize the recording of demographic and help-seeking information, introduce matters and rules during the consultation process, read and confirm the consultation agreement and confidentiality exceptions, check for omissions and unclear items, ensure the completeness, accuracy of the data, and informed consent.
390.when_to_use: During the diagnostic assessment and record-keeping phase of the first consultation, when starting systematic data collection.
390.trigger: When the visitor has not yet provided structured data or is unclear about the consultation process and rules, basic information needs to be registered and the agreement confirmed.

343.skill_name: Administer and record psychological test results
343.skill_description: Administer and record key scores and factors from scales such as SCL-90, EPQ, SAS, or SDS with the client's consent, quantify symptom intensity and range, establish an assessment baseline for assisting diagnosis and follow-up comparison, and provide preliminary analysis feedback to the client.
343.when_to_use: During the initial consultation or re-evaluation phase, when quantifying symptoms and establishing a baseline after completing the clinical interview.
343.trigger: Client consent to undergo psychological testing, or need for objective assessment of symptoms such as obsession, anxiety, etc., and subsequent comparison.

435.skill_name: Collect medication history and family psychiatric history
435.skill_description: Fill in past consultation and treatment experiences (such as specialist diagnosis of phobias), medication use and reasons for discontinuation due to side effects, and record family psychiatric history (such as no family history of mental illness), for risk and feasibility assessment, and to support diagnosis and plan formulation.
435.when_to_use: When filling out medical history items on the initial consultation form, or when conducting a safety assessment before developing an intervention plan.
435.trigger: When the visitor mentions past medical visits, medication intolerance, or is asked about family psychiatric illness history.

375.skill_name: Verify and supplement medical and family history with relatives or classmates
375.skill_description: Verify and record past physical medical history, personal development history, and family psychiatric history with relatives or classmates to form multi-source data, improve information accuracy and completeness, and avoid bias from a single source.
375.when_to_use: When self-reported information needs verification or supplementation, especially concerning key medical history and family history.
375.trigger: When the client's information is limited or there are questions, third-party corroboration and supplementation are needed.

385.skill_name: Coordinate physical examination and record conclusions to rule out organic causes
385.skill_description: Recommend and arrange medical examinations based on assessment needs, record examination conclusions in the record (e.g., no obvious organic disease), to rule out organic mental disorders and complete diagnostic evidence, to avoid misdiagnosis.
385.when_to_use: Assessment and diagnosis stage, when ruling out organic causes or completing diagnostic evidence is needed.
385.trigger: Patient has recurrent somatic symptoms or concerns about organic issues.

376.skill_name: Review physical examination data and record exclusion conclusions
376.skill_description: Review past physical examination and relevant test results and record conclusions (such as no physical disease found), or note normal/abnormal physical examination, to support psychological diagnosis and etiology differentiation and guide subsequent intervention.
376.when_to_use: When conducting initial assessment to differentiate psychological and somatic causes, making a preliminary diagnosis, or deciding the subsequent intervention path.
376.trigger: Past history mentions physical examination, or suspicion that physical factors may affect current symptoms.

291.skill_description: Select scales such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, and EPQ for assessment, record total scores and dimension scores according to validity and standards, quantify anxiety, depression, and related factor levels, and save as baseline and follow-up comparison data sources.
291.when_to_use: During the initial assessment phase or diagnostic phase, when quantifying symptoms and establishing test baselines.
291.trigger: Test results have been issued and are valid, or there is a chief complaint of anxiety/depression and related issues requiring standardized scale assessment.
